counselingAdvice: Use sparingly. One fingertip unit covers an area twice the size of an adult hand. Do not cover with airtight dressings unless advised by doctor.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in viral, fungal, or untreated bacterial skin infections, rosacea, perioral dermatitis, and acne.
adverseEffects: Skin atrophy, telangiectasia, striae, secondary skin infection, contact dermatitis.
monitoringAdvice: Inspect skin for atrophy; limit continuous duration to 2-4 weeks.

name: Finacea (Azelaic acid) 15% Gel (30 g)
defaultDirections: Wash and dry face gently, then apply thinly to affected areas TWICE daily morning and evening.

commonDoses.label: Papulopustular Rosacea / Acne
commonDoses.directions: Apply to clean, dry skin twice daily. May reduce to once daily if irritation occurs.

warningNote: Transient mild burning, stinging, or redness is common during the first 2-4 weeks. Improves with continued use.
indication: Treatment of papulopustular rosacea and mild to moderate acne vulgaris.
mechanismOfAction: Exerts anti-inflammatory effects by reducing reactive oxygen species, normalises keratinisation to clear comedones, and displays antimicrobial activity against Cutibacterium acnes.
pbsRestrictionNote: Private prescription medicine in Australia.
counselingAdvice: Wash skin with gentle soap-free cleanser before applying. If irritation occurs, use once daily in the evening until tolerated.
cautionsAndContraindications: Avoid contact with eyes, mouth, and mucous membranes.
adverseEffects: Local burning, stinging, itching, dry skin, peeling, erythema.
monitoringAdvice: Assess clinical response after 4-8 weeks.

name: Xalatan (Latanoprost) 50 mcg / mL (0.005%) Eye Drops (2.5 mL)
defaultDirections: Instil ONE drop into the affected eye(s) ONCE daily in the evening.

commonDoses.label: Glaucoma / Ocular Hypertension
commonDoses.directions: Instil 1 drop into affected eye(s) once daily in the evening.

warningNote: May cause permanent gradual darkening of eye iris color (browning) and increased eyelash length, thickness, and pigmentation.
indication: Reduction of elevated intraocular pressure in patients with open-angle glaucoma and ocular hypertension.
mechanismOfAction: Selective prostanoid FP receptor agonist that increases the uveoscleral outflow of aqueous humor, reducing intraocular pressure.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS Subsidised for open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension.
counselingAdvice: Remove contact lenses before instilling and wait 15 minutes before reinserting. Apply pressure to inner tear duct for 1 minute after drop to reduce systemic absorption.
cautionsAndContraindications: Caution in active intraocular inflammation (uveitis) and patients at risk of macular oedema.
adverseEffects: Iris hyperpigmentation, eyelash changes, conjunctival hyperemia, ocular irritation, punctate keratitis.
monitoringAdvice: Regular intraocular pressure (IOP) measurement and visual field testing by optometrist/ophthalmologist.
storageAdvice: Store unopened bottle in refrigerator (2°C - 8°C). Once opened, store below 25°C for up to 4 weeks.

name: Eliquis (Apixaban) 5 mg Tablet
drugClass: Direct Oral Anticoagulant (DOAC) / Factor Xa Inhibitor
defaultDirections: Take ONE tablet TWICE daily with or without food. Do not skip doses.

commonDoses.label: Non-valvular Atrial Fibrillation (Standard)
commonDoses.directions: Take 5mg twice daily with or without food.

commonDoses.label: Dose reduction criteria (2.5mg twice daily)
commonDoses.directions: Take 2.5mg twice daily if meeting >=2 of: age >=80, weight <=60kg, creatinine >=133.

warningNote: Bleeding Risk: Do not stop taking without consulting doctor (markedly increased stroke risk). Withhold 24-48 hours before elective surgery.
indication: Prevention of stroke and systemic embolism in adult patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation, and treatment/prevention of DVT and pulmonary embolism.
mechanismOfAction: Potent, direct, highly selective, reversible inhibitor of both free and clot-bound Factor Xa and prothrombinase activity, prolonging clotting times.
pbsRestrictionNote: Non-valvular atrial fibrillation with at least one additional stroke risk factor, or DVT/PE.
counselingAdvice: Take at the same times morning and night. Do not miss doses. Watch for signs of serious bleeding (dark black stools, blood in urine, unexplained bruising).
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in clinically significant active bleeding and severe hepatic disease. Caution with concurrent NSAIDs or antiplatelets.
adverseEffects: Haemorrhage/bleeding (epistaxis, GI bleeding, haematuria), anaemia, contusion.
monitoringAdvice: Baseline and annual renal function (eGFR), full blood count, and liver function.

name: Anginine (Glyceryl trinitrate) 600 mcg (0.6 mg) Sublingual Tablet (100 tablets)
defaultDirections: Dissolve ONE tablet under the tongue at the first sign of chest pain. If pain persists after 5 minutes, call 000 ambulance.

commonDoses.label: Acute angina relief
commonDoses.directions: Dissolve 1/2 to 1 tablet under tongue sitting down. Repeat in 5m if needed; call 000 if pain persists.

warningNote: ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATION WITH PDE5 INHIBITORS (Viagra, Cialis). Sit down before taking (can cause sudden low blood pressure and fainting).
indication: Prophylaxis and treatment of acute angina pectoris episodes.
mechanismOfAction: Releases nitric oxide in vascular smooth muscle, stimulating cGMP and causing preferential systemic venous dilatation, reducing cardiac preload and myocardial oxygen demand.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS Subsidised for angina relief.
counselingAdvice: Sit down before taking because it can make you dizzy. Dissolve under tongue; do not swallow whole. Discard bottle 3 months after opening.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated with PDE5 inhibitors (sildenafil, tadalafil), severe hypotension, and elevated intracranial pressure.
adverseEffects: Throbbing headache, postural hypotension, reflex tachycardia, facial flushing.
monitoringAdvice: Replace bottle every 3 months; monitor angina frequency and response.
storageAdvice: Store below 25°C in the original glass bottle with cap tightly closed.

name: Ferro-grad C (Dried ferrous sulfate + Sodium ascorbate (Vitamin C)) 325 mg (105 mg elemental iron) / 500 mg Filmtab Tablet
generic: Dried ferrous sulfate + Sodium ascorbate (Vitamin C)
defaultFrequency: Once daily on an empty stomach
defaultDirections: Take ONE tablet ONCE daily on an empty stomach (1 hour before or 2 hours after meals). May take with food if stomach upset occurs.

commonDoses.label: Iron deficiency anaemia treatment
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet daily with water for 3 to 6 months to replenish stores.

warningNote: Keep out of reach of children (iron overdose is fatal in young children). Expect dark/black stools (harmless).
indication: Prevention and treatment of iron deficiency anaemia.
mechanismOfAction: Provides essential elemental iron incorporated into haemoglobin, myoglobin, and key respiratory enzymes; ascorbic acid maintains iron in the absorbable ferrous (Fe2+) state.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS Subsidised for documented iron deficiency anaemia.
counselingAdvice: Swallow whole; do not suck or chew. Stools will turn black; this is normal. Do not take with tea, coffee, milk, or calcium within 2 hours.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in hemochromatosis and conditions with impaired iron utilization.
adverseEffects: Constipation, dark stools, nausea, abdominal discomfort, diarrhoea.
monitoringAdvice: Full blood count and serum ferritin after 8-12 weeks of treatment.

name: Keflex (Cefalexin) 500 mg Capsule
defaultDirections: Take ONE capsule FOUR times daily (every 6 hours) with water for 5 to 7 days.
indication: Respiratory tract infections, otitis media, skin and soft tissue infections, bone infections, and genitourinary tract infections.
mechanismOfAction: Binds to penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs), inhibiting bacterial cell wall peptidoglycan synthesis.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS Subsidised for approved bacterial infections.
counselingAdvice: Take at evenly spaced intervals around the clock. Complete full course. Can be taken with or without food.
cautionsAndContraindications: Caution in patients with severe penicillin allergy (anaphylaxis history - cross-reactivity risk).
adverseEffects: Diarrhoea, nausea, dyspepsia, abdominal cramps, rash, eosinophilia.
monitoringAdvice: Assess clinical response; check renal function in severe impairment.

name: Amoxil (Amoxicillin) 500 mg Capsule
defaultDirections: Take ONE capsule THREE times daily (every 8 hours) with water for 5 to 7 days.
indication: Ear, nose, and throat infections, community-acquired respiratory tract infections, and uncomplicated gonorrhoea.
mechanismOfAction: Inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis during active replication by binding to PBPs.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS Subsidised for susceptible bacterial infections.
counselingAdvice: Take every 8 hours with or without food. Complete the entire course. Report severe watery diarrhoea immediately.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in penicillin hypersensitivity and infectious mononucleosis (high risk of rash).
adverseEffects: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, skin rash, pruritus.
monitoringAdvice: Check for allergic skin reactions; monitor renal function with prolonged high doses.

name: Zithromax (Azithromycin) 500 mg Tablet
defaultDirections: Take ONE tablet ONCE daily for 3 consecutive days, at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after food.
indication: Community-acquired pneumonia, acute bacterial exacerbations of COPD, chlamydial urethritis and cervicitis, and trachoma.
mechanismOfAction: Reversibly binds to the 50S ribosomal subunit of susceptible microorganisms, inhibiting transpeptidation.
pbsRestrictionNote: Chlamydia trachomatis, atypical pneumonia, or cystic fibrosis prophylaxis.
counselingAdvice: Take on an empty stomach with a full glass of water. Space antacids containing aluminium or magnesium by at least 2 hours.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in history of cholestatic jaundice or hepatic dysfunction associated with prior azithromycin. QT prolongation risk.
adverseEffects: Diarrhoea, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, transient hearing impairment with high doses.
monitoringAdvice: Assess resolution of infection; monitor ECG in patients with cardiac conduction disorders.

name: Noroxin (Norfloxacin) 400 mg Tablet
defaultDirections: Take ONE tablet TWICE daily on an empty stomach with a full glass of water for 3 to 7 days.
indication: Uncomplicated and complicated urinary tract infections and bacterial gastroenteritis caused by susceptible pathogens.
mechanismOfAction: Inhibits bacterial topoisomerase II (DNA gyrase) and topoisomerase IV, disrupting bacterial DNA supercoiling and replication.
pbsRestrictionNote: Urinary tract infections refractory to first-line agents.
counselingAdvice: Drink plenty of water. Take 1 hour before or 2 hours after meals, milk, or iron supplements. Stop taking if tendon pain occurs.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in children, growing adolescents, pregnancy, and history of quinolone-induced tendinopathy.
adverseEffects: Nausea, headache, dizziness, tendonitis, photosensitivity.
monitoringAdvice: Monitor for tendon pain; assess renal function.

name: Dalacin C (Clindamycin) 150 mg Capsule
defaultDirections: Take ONE to TWO capsules FOUR times daily (every 6 hours) with a full glass of water while sitting upright.
indication: Serious infections caused by susceptible anaerobic bacteria, and streptococcal and staphylococcal infections in penicillin-allergic patients.
mechanismOfAction: Binds to the 50S ribosomal subunit of bacteria, preventing peptide bond formation and protein synthesis.
pbsRestrictionNote: Penicillin-allergic patients with serious staphylococcal or anaerobic infections.
counselingAdvice: Always swallow with a full glass of water to avoid throat irritation. If severe watery diarrhoea develops, stop immediately and contact your doctor.
cautionsAndContraindications: High risk of Clostridioides difficile-associated pseudomembranous colitis. Contraindicated in history of antibiotic-associated colitis.
adverseEffects: Diarrhoea, pseudomembranous colitis, nausea, vomiting, skin rash, oesophagitis.
monitoringAdvice: Monitor bowel habit; test for C. difficile toxin if persistent diarrhoea develops.

name: Lamisil (Terbinafine) 250 mg Tablet
defaultDirections: Take ONE tablet ONCE daily with water for 6 weeks (fingernails) to 12 weeks (toenails).
indication: Fungal infections of the fingernails and toenails (onychomycosis) and severe tinea pedis/corporis unresponsive to topical therapy.
mechanismOfAction: Selectively inhibits fungal squalene epoxidase, blocking ergosterol biosynthesis and causing intracellular accumulation of toxic squalene.
pbsRestrictionNote: Onychomycosis confirmed by microscopy or culture.
counselingAdvice: Takes several months for new healthy nail to grow out. Report dark urine, pale stools, yellowing of eyes, or persistent nausea immediately.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in chronic or active hepatic disease. Caution in psoriasis or lupus erythematosus.
adverseEffects: Taste disturbance (dysgeusia/ageusia), gastrointestinal fullness, loss of appetite, headache, rash, rare severe hepatotoxicity.
monitoringAdvice: Baseline liver function tests (LFTs) and repeat after 4 to 6 weeks of treatment.

name: Tamiflu (Oseltamivir) 75 mg Capsule
defaultDirections: Take ONE capsule TWICE daily with food for 5 days. Must be initiated within 48 hours of influenza symptom onset.
indication: Treatment and post-exposure prophylaxis of uncomplicated influenza A and B illness in patients presenting within 48 hours of first symptoms.
mechanismOfAction: Inhibits influenza virus neuraminidase, preventing the release and spread of newly formed virions from infected host cells.
pbsRestrictionNote: Influenza infection in high-risk immunocompromised or institutionalized patients.
counselingAdvice: Take with food to minimize nausea. Complete the full 5-day course. Start as soon as possible after flu symptoms begin.
cautionsAndContraindications: Dose reduction required in renal impairment (eGFR < 60 mL/min).
adverseEffects: Nausea, vomiting, headache, abdominal pain, rare neuropsychiatric events (hallucinations, confusion in adolescents).
monitoringAdvice: Monitor for symptom resolution and acute behavioural changes in adolescents.

name: Ventolin (Salbutamol) 100 mcg per actuation Pressurised Inhalation (200 doses)
defaultDirections: Inhale ONE to TWO puffs as needed for sudden wheezing, shortness of breath, or before exercise (Max 8 puffs/24h).
indication: Relief of acute bronchospasm in asthma and other conditions with reversible airways obstruction; prophylaxis of exercise-induced asthma.
mechanismOfAction: Stimulates beta2-adrenergic receptors in bronchial smooth muscle, activating adenylate cyclase, increasing cAMP, and inducing rapid bronchodilation.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS Subsidised for reversible obstructive airways disease.
counselingAdvice: Shake well before use. Use a spacer device for better lung delivery. If requiring more than 2-3 times per week, asthma is poorly controlled; see your GP.
cautionsAndContraindications: Caution in thyrotoxicosis, tachyarrhythmias, and severe hypertension.
adverseEffects: Fine skeletal muscle tremor (especially hands), tachycardia, palpitations, headache, peripheral vasodilation.
monitoringAdvice: Frequency of reliever use (marker of overall asthma control); check inhaler and spacer technique.

name: Seretide Accuhaler (Fluticasone propionate + Salmeterol) 250 mcg / 50 mcg Dry Powder Inhalation (60 doses)
defaultDirections: Inhale ONE blister inhalation TWICE daily morning and night. Rinse mouth with water and spit out after use.
indication: Regular maintenance treatment of asthma where combination therapy is appropriate, and symptomatic treatment of severe COPD.
mechanismOfAction: Fluticasone suppresses airway inflammation; salmeterol selectively stimulates beta2 receptors, providing prolonged 12-hour bronchodilatation.
pbsRestrictionNote: Asthma uncontrolled on ICS monotherapy, or severe COPD.
counselingAdvice: Hold horizontal, slide lever until it clicks, breathe out fully away from device, inhale deeply through mouthpiece. Rinse mouth with water and spit out.
cautionsAndContraindications: Caution in pulmonary tuberculosis, fungal airway infections, and cardiac arrhythmias.
adverseEffects: Oral candidiasis, dysphonia, throat irritation, headache, palpitations, muscle cramps.
monitoringAdvice: Check dose counter; review FEV1 and exacerbation frequency.
storageAdvice: Store below 30°C in a dry place.

name: Breo Ellipta (Fluticasone furoate + Vilanterol) 100 mcg / 25 mcg Dry Powder Inhalation (30 doses)
defaultDirections: Inhale ONE inhalation ONCE daily at the same time each day. Rinse mouth with water and spit out.
indication: Maintenance treatment of asthma in patients aged 12 and older, and maintenance treatment of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD).
mechanismOfAction: Synthetic trifluorinated corticosteroid with high affinity for glucocorticoid receptor combined with vilanterol, a 24-hour ultra-LABA.
pbsRestrictionNote: Patients with asthma or COPD uncontrolled on lower therapy.
counselingAdvice: Slide cover down until click is heard. Inhale deeply, hold breath 3-4 seconds. Dose counter decrements by 1. Rinse mouth and spit out.
cautionsAndContraindications: Caution in severe hepatic impairment and unstable cardiovascular disease.
adverseEffects: Nasopharyngitis, upper respiratory tract infection, oral candidiasis, dysphonia, headache.
monitoringAdvice: Assess adherence with convenient once-daily dosing; monitor lung function.
storageAdvice: Store below 30°C in original moisture-protective tray.

name: Singulair (Montelukast) 10 mg Tablet
defaultDirections: Take ONE tablet ONCE daily in the evening with or without food.
indication: Prophylaxis and chronic treatment of asthma, relief of symptoms of seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis, and prevention of exercise-induced bronchoconstriction.
mechanismOfAction: High-affinity selective antagonist at CysLT1 cysteinyl leukotriene receptors, inhibiting leukotriene-mediated bronchoconstriction, vascular permeability, and mucosal edema.
pbsRestrictionNote: Add-on therapy in asthma uncontrolled on ICS.
warningNote: TGA Neuropsychiatric Alert: Monitor for behavioural changes, vivid dreams, nightmares, aggression, depression, or suicidal ideation.
counselingAdvice: Take in the evening. Must be taken daily for asthma control, even during symptom-free periods. Stop and see doctor if unusual mood or sleep changes occur.
cautionsAndContraindications: Not indicated for the reversal of acute bronchospasm during an asthma attack.
adverseEffects: Upper respiratory infection, headache, abdominal pain, dream abnormalities, neuropsychiatric changes.
monitoringAdvice: Clinical monitoring for neuropsychiatric symptoms at every prescription review.

name: Nasonex (Mometasone furoate) 50 mcg per actuation Nasal Spray (140 sprays)
defaultDirections: Blow nose gently, then spray TWO sprays into EACH nostril ONCE daily in the morning.
indication: Treatment and prophylaxis of symptoms of seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis, and treatment of nasal polyps in adults.
mechanismOfAction: Exerts local anti-inflammatory and vasoconstrictive activity on the nasal mucosa with negligible systemic bioavailability (<1%).
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS Subsidised for severe allergic rhinitis.
counselingAdvice: Prime bottle before first use. Aim tip slightly away from middle nasal septum towards ear. Regular daily use for 1-2 weeks provides maximum relief.
cautionsAndContraindications: Caution in untreated nasal candida or herpes simplex, recent nasal surgery, or septal perforation.
adverseEffects: Epistaxis (nosebleed), pharyngitis, nasal burning, headache, sneezing.
monitoringAdvice: Inspect nasal septum for mucosal atrophy with prolonged multi-year treatment.

name: Telfast (Fexofenadine) 180 mg Tablet
defaultDirections: Take ONE tablet ONCE daily with water.
indication: Relief of symptoms of seasonal allergic rhinitis (hayfever) and chronic idiopathic urticaria (hives).
mechanismOfAction: Selective peripheral H1-receptor antagonist with minimal blood-brain barrier penetration, lacking anticholinergic or alpha1-adrenergic blocking activity.
pbsRestrictionNote: OTC / Private prescription in Australia.
counselingAdvice: Non-drowsy formulation. Take with water; avoid taking with grapefruit, orange, or apple juice as fruit juices reduce absorption.
cautionsAndContraindications: Caution in elderly and patients with renal impairment.
adverseEffects: Headache, drowsiness (rare), nausea, dry mouth.
monitoringAdvice: Assess symptom relief of allergic rhinitis or urticaria.

name: Somac (Pantoprazole) 40 mg Enteric Coated Tablet
defaultDirections: Take ONE tablet ONCE daily in the morning, 30 minutes before breakfast. Swallow whole.
indication: Duodenal ulcer, gastric ulcer, moderate to severe reflux oesophagitis, and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome.
mechanismOfAction: Pro-drug activated in acid canaliculi of gastric parietal cells, irreversibly inhibiting H+/K+-ATPase enzyme.
pbsRestrictionNote: GORD, peptic ulcer, or gastroprotection in high-risk NSAID users.
counselingAdvice: Swallow whole with water; do not crush or chew. Take 30 minutes before your morning meal. Re-assess ongoing clinical need periodically.
cautionsAndContraindications: Lowest CYP2C19 interaction among PPIs (safer with clopidogrel than omeprazole). Caution with long-term use.
adverseEffects: Headache, diarrhoea, nausea, flatulence, abdominal pain, hypomagnesaemia with multi-year use.
monitoringAdvice: Magnesium and vitamin B12 levels in long-term therapy (>12 months).

name: Maxolon (Metoclopramide) 10 mg Tablet
defaultDirections: Take ONE tablet THREE times daily, 30 minutes before meals (Max 5 days duration).
indication: Relief of nausea and vomiting, diabetic gastroparesis, and diagnostic radiology of the gastrointestinal tract.
mechanismOfAction: Antagonises central D2 dopamine receptors in the CTZ, and stimulates upper GI tract motility by enhancing acetylcholine release.
pbsRestrictionNote: Short-term management of nausea and vomiting.
warningNote: TGA Alert: Risk of neurological adverse events (extrapyramidal disorders, acute dystonia, tardive dyskinesia). Limit treatment to maximum 5 days.
counselingAdvice: Take 30 minutes before food. Do not take for more than 5 days. Stop immediately and seek medical attention if facial muscle spasms or restless twitching occurs.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in gastrointestinal bleeding, mechanical bowel obstruction, perforation, and phaeochromocytoma.
adverseEffects: Drowsiness, restlessness, fatigue, acute dystonic reactions (oculogyric crisis, torticollis), diarrhoea.
monitoringAdvice: Monitor for extrapyramidal symptoms, particularly in young adults and elderly.

name: Coloxyl with Senna (Docusate sodium + Sennoside B) 50 mg / 8 mg Tablet
defaultDirections: Take ONE to TWO tablets at night with a full glass of water.
indication: Treatment of constipation, particularly opioid-induced constipation, post-surgical, or bed-ridden patients.
mechanismOfAction: Docusate acts as an anionic surfactant, reducing surface tension and facilitating water entry into stool; sennosides stimulate colonic peristalsis.
pbsRestrictionNote: Paraplegic or quadriplegic patients, opioid-induced constipation in palliative care.
counselingAdvice: Drink plenty of water throughout the day. May take 6 to 12 hours to work (usually works the following morning).
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in undiagnosed abdominal pain, nausea/vomiting, intestinal obstruction, or acute appendicitis.
adverseEffects: Abdominal cramps, griping, diarrhoea, melanosis coli (with prolonged chronic use).
monitoringAdvice: Assess bowel regularity; encourage dietary fiber and adequate hydration.

name: Movicol (Macrogol 3350 + Electrolytes) 13.125 g Powder for Oral Solution Sachet (30 sachets)
form: Powder for Oral Solution Sachet (30 sachets)
defaultDirections: Dissolve ONE sachet in 125 mL of water and drink ONCE to THREE times daily as needed.
indication: Chronic constipation and treatment of faecal impaction.
mechanismOfAction: Macrogol 3350 acts as an osmotic agent, retaining water in the bowel lumen to hydrate, soften, and increase stool volume without electrolyte shift.
pbsRestrictionNote: Chronic constipation refractory to other treatments or faecal impaction.
counselingAdvice: Dissolve the powder completely in half a glass of water before drinking. Reconstituted solution can be refrigerated and used within 24 hours.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in intestinal perforation, obstruction, toxic megacolon, and severe inflammatory bowel conditions.
adverseEffects: Abdominal distension, borborygmi, nausea, mild diarrhoea.
monitoringAdvice: Maintain adequate hydration during treatment.

name: Salofalk (Mesalazine) 1000 mg (1 g) Granules Sachet / Tablet
defaultDirections: Take ONE to THREE sachets ONCE daily in the morning with water. Do NOT chew the granules.
indication: Treatment and maintenance of remission in mild to moderate Ulcerative Colitis.
mechanismOfAction: Locally inhibits intestinal cyclooxygenase, lipoxygenase, and pro-inflammatory cytokine production in the colonic mucosa.
pbsRestrictionNote: Ulcerative colitis confirmed by endoscopy.
counselingAdvice: Pour granules onto tongue and wash down with plenty of water without chewing, ensuring intact delivery to the colon.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in severe renal or hepatic impairment, and salicylate hypersensitivity.
adverseEffects: Headache, nausea, abdominal pain, diarrhea, interstitial nephritis (rare).
monitoringAdvice: Check renal function (creatinine, eGFR) and urine protein before initiation and every 6-12 months.

name: Targin (Oxycodone + Naloxone) 10 mg / 5 mg Controlled-Release Tablet
drugClass: Opioid Agonist + Opioid Antagonist Fixed-Dose Combination
defaultDirections: Take ONE tablet TWICE daily strictly every 12 hours with water. Swallow whole; do NOT crush, break, or chew.
indication: Severe chronic pain of malignant or non-malignant origin requiring around-the-clock opioid analgesia; naloxone prevents opioid-induced constipation.
mechanismOfAction: Oxycodone provides central analgesia; naloxone has high first-pass hepatic metabolism (>97%), locally blocking intestinal opioid receptors and preventing constipation without reversing analgesia.
pbsRestrictionNote: Severe chronic disabling pain unresponsive to non-opioid analgesics.
warningNote: CRUSHING IS FATAL: Chewing or crushing releases fatal dose of oxycodone immediately. S8 Controlled Drug subject to real-time SafeScript checks.
counselingAdvice: Swallow whole; never cut, crush, or chew. Take every 12 hours with or without food. Avoid alcohol completely.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in severe hepatic impairment (naloxone enters systemic circulation and blocks analgesia), respiratory depression, and acute abdomen.
adverseEffects: Nausea, dizziness, headache, somnolence, sweating, hot flushes.
monitoringAdvice: Check SafeScript; review pain scores, functional goals, and signs of opioid tolerance.
storageAdvice: Store below 25°C in secure locked cabinet.

name: Norspan (Buprenorphine) 10 mcg / hour (10 mg patch) Transdermal 7-Day Patch (2 patches)
defaultDirections: Apply ONE patch to clean, hairless, intact skin. Replace with a new patch on a different site every 7 days.
indication: Management of chronic severe non-malignant and cancer pain unresponsive to non-narcotic analgesics.
mechanismOfAction: High-affinity partial agonist at mu-opioid receptors and antagonist at kappa receptors, slowly dissociating to provide prolonged 7-day analgesic action.
pbsRestrictionNote: Chronic severe disabling pain where alternative analgesia is ineffective.
warningNote: Schedule 8 Controlled Drug: Do not expose patch to external heat sources (heating pads, electric blankets, saunas, hot tubs - accelerates drug release).
counselingAdvice: Apply to non-irritated, hairless skin on upper outer arm, upper chest, or back. Rotate application site and do not reuse the same site for at least 3-4 weeks.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in severe respiratory depression and acute pain.
adverseEffects: Application site erythema and pruritus, nausea, dizziness, somnolence, constipation.
monitoringAdvice: Inspect skin site; verify patch adhesion; check SafeScript.

name: Epilim Chrono (Sodium valproate) 500 mg Controlled Release Tablet
defaultDirections: Take ONE tablet TWICE daily with food. Swallow whole.
indication: Treatment of generalised, partial, and absence seizures, and treatment of manic episodes associated with bipolar disorder.
mechanismOfAction: Increases brain concentrations of GABA by inhibiting GABA transaminase and blocking voltage-dependent sodium and T-type calcium channels.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS Subsidised for epilepsy and bipolar disorder.
warningNote: TERATOGENICITY BLACK BOX WARNING: High risk of major congenital malformations (10%) and neurodevelopmental disorders (30-40%). Contraindicated in women of childbearing potential unless strict pregnancy prevention program.
counselingAdvice: Take with food. Swallow whole. Women of childbearing age must use highly effective contraception and discuss pregnancy plans with doctor well in advance.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in active liver disease, personal/family history of severe hepatic dysfunction, and mitochondrial disorders (POLG mutations).
adverseEffects: Weight gain, tremor, hair thinning/alopecia, nausea, menstrual irregularities, thrombocytopenia.
monitoringAdvice: Baseline and periodic LFTs, full blood count, platelet count, and serum valproate levels if toxicity suspected.

name: Keppra (Levetiracetam) 500 mg Tablet
defaultDirections: Take ONE tablet TWICE daily with water, with or without food.
indication: Monotherapy and adjunctive therapy in partial onset seizures with or without secondary generalisation, and myoclonic seizures in idiopathic generalised epilepsy.
mechanismOfAction: Selectively binds to synaptic vesicle protein 2A (SV2A) in presynaptic terminals, inhibiting presynaptic calcium channels and modulating neurotransmitter exocytosis.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS Subsidised for epilepsy management.
counselingAdvice: Take at regular 12-hour intervals morning and night. Do NOT stop taking suddenly as this can precipitate rebound seizures. Report mood or behavioural changes.
cautionsAndContraindications: Dose reduction mandatory in renal impairment. Caution in patients with history of depression or psychiatric illness.
adverseEffects: Somnolence, asthenia, dizziness, behavioral changes (irritability, agitation, depression).
monitoringAdvice: Renal function (eGFR); screen for psychiatric symptoms and suicidal ideation.

name: Madopar (Levodopa + Benserazide) 100 mg / 25 mg Capsule
defaultFrequency: Three times daily, 30 min before meals
defaultDirections: Take ONE capsule THREE times daily, 30 minutes before meals or 1 hour after meals.
indication: Treatment of Parkinson's disease and symptomatic parkinsonism.
mechanismOfAction: Levodopa crosses the blood-brain barrier and is decarboxylated into dopamine in the striatum; benserazide blocks peripheral decarboxylation, preventing nausea and increasing brain availability.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS Subsidised for Parkinson's disease.
counselingAdvice: Take at least 30 minutes before meals or 1 hour after, because dietary protein competes with levodopa for intestinal absorption. Take doses at consistent scheduled times.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated with non-selective MAO inhibitors, severe endocrine, cardiac or psychiatric disorders, and narrow-angle glaucoma.
adverseEffects: Nausea, involuntary movements (dyskinesias), postural hypotension, vivid dreams, hallucinations, impulse control disorders.
monitoringAdvice: Assess motor fluctuations (on-off phenomena, wearing-off); check for orthostatic hypotension.
storageAdvice: Store below 25°C in original container with desiccant.

name: Zoloft (Sertraline) 50 mg Tablet
defaultDirections: Take ONE tablet ONCE daily in the morning or evening with food. Do not stop abruptly.
indication: Major depressive disorder, obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), panic disorder, post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), and social phobia.
mechanismOfAction: Potent and selective inhibitor of neuronal serotonin (5-HT) reuptake, with minimal effect on noradrenaline and dopamine transporters.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS Subsidised for depression and anxiety disorders.
counselingAdvice: Take with food to reduce nausea. May take 2-4 weeks to feel improvement. Do not stop taking this medicine without discussing with doctor.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated with MAOIs or pimozide. Risk of serotonin syndrome with triptans, tramadol, or St John's Wort.
adverseEffects: Gastrointestinal upset (diarrhoea, nausea), insomnia, sexual dysfunction, tremor, dry mouth.
monitoringAdvice: Mental health review at 2 and 4 weeks; monitor electrolytes (hyponatremia risk in elderly).

name: Avanza (Mirtazapine) 30 mg Tablet / SolTab (Orally Disintegrating)
defaultDirections: Take ONE tablet ONCE daily at bedtime with water.
indication: Treatment of major depressive episodes, particularly with co-morbid insomnia, severe anxiety, and weight loss.
mechanismOfAction: Antagonises central presynaptic alpha2-auto and hetero-receptors, increasing central noradrenaline and serotonin release; blocks 5-HT2 and 5-HT3 receptors and H1 histamine receptors (causing sedation).
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS Subsidised for major depression.
counselingAdvice: Take at bedtime as it causes significant sleepiness. May increase appetite and cause weight gain. Full antidepressant effect takes 2-4 weeks.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated with MAO inhibitors (14-day washout). Caution in epilepsy and narrow-angle glaucoma.
adverseEffects: Sedation, increased appetite, weight gain, dry mouth, dizziness, constipation.
monitoringAdvice: Monitor body weight, lipid panel, and blood glucose; review depressive symptoms.

name: Seroquel (Quetiapine) 25 mg Tablet
defaultDirections: Take ONE tablet ONCE daily at bedtime with or without food.
indication: Treatment of schizophrenia, bipolar mania and depression, and adjunctive treatment of major depressive disorder.
mechanismOfAction: Antagonist at multiple neurotransmitter receptors including brain serotonin 5-HT2 and dopamine D1 and D2 receptors; potent H1 antagonist.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS Subsidised for schizophrenia and bipolar disorder.
warningNote: Monitored Medicine (SafeScript). Significant metabolic side effects (rapid weight gain, dyslipidaemia, impaired glucose tolerance) and sedation.
counselingAdvice: Take at bedtime. Avoid alcohol. Stand up slowly from sitting or lying down to prevent dizziness or fainting.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated with active central nervous system depression. Caution in elderly with dementia (increased mortality risk).
adverseEffects: Somnolence, orthostatic hypotension, weight gain, dry mouth, constipation, elevated cholesterol and triglycerides.
monitoringAdvice: Baseline and regular fasting glucose, HbA1c, fasting lipids, weight/BMI, and blood pressure.

name: Circadin (Melatonin) 2 mg Prolonged-Release Tablet
defaultDirections: Take ONE tablet ONCE daily 1 to 2 hours before bedtime after food. Swallow whole.
indication: Short-term treatment of primary insomnia characterised by poor quality of sleep in patients who are aged 55 or over.
mechanismOfAction: Activates MT1 and MT2 G-protein coupled receptors in the suprachiasmatic nucleus, mimicking endogenous melatonin and regulating circadian sleep-wake cycles.
pbsRestrictionNote: Private prescription in Australia.
counselingAdvice: Take 1 to 2 hours before bed after food. Swallow whole; do not crush or chew. Practice good sleep habits (dark, quiet room, no screens).
cautionsAndContraindications: Caution in autoimmune diseases and severe hepatic impairment. Avoid alcohol.
adverseEffects: Headache, nasopharyngitis, back pain, arthralgia, vivid dreams.
monitoringAdvice: Review sleep quality and daytime alertness after 3 weeks.

name: Estradot (Estradiol (17-beta)) 50 mcg / 24 hours (0.78 mg patch) Transdermal Matrix Patch (8 patches = 4 weeks)
defaultDirections: Apply ONE patch to clean, dry, hairless skin below the waistline. Replace twice weekly on the same two days each week.
indication: Hormone replacement therapy for oestrogen deficiency symptoms (hot flushes, night sweats, sleep disturbance, mood changes) in postmenopausal women.
mechanismOfAction: Transdermally delivers natural 17-beta estradiol directly into the systemic circulation without hepatic first-pass metabolism, activating oestrogen receptors.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS Subsidised for menopausal hormone replacement therapy.
warningNote: Intact Uterus Requirement: Women with an intact uterus MUST also take a progestogen (e.g. Prometrium) for at least 12-14 days per month to prevent endometrial cancer.
counselingAdvice: Apply below the waist (buttocks or lower abdomen). NEVER apply on or near the breasts. Press firmly for 10 seconds. Change twice a week on the same days.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in history of breast cancer, oestrogen-dependent neoplasia, active DVT/PE, arterial thromboembolic disease, and unexplained vaginal bleeding.
adverseEffects: Breast tenderness, application site redness/itching, headache, bloating, nausea.
monitoringAdvice: Annual clinical review; mammography and cervical screening; blood pressure check.

name: Prometrium (Progesterone (Micronised)) 100 mg Soft Capsule (30 capsules)
defaultDirections: Take ONE to TWO capsules ONCE daily at bedtime with a glass of water, on an empty stomach.
indication: Endometrial protection in postmenopausal women receiving oestrogen hormone replacement therapy (HRT).
mechanismOfAction: Induces secretory transformation in an oestrogen-primed endometrium, inhibiting proliferative action of oestrogen and preventing endometrial hyperplasia.
pbsRestrictionNote: Postmenopausal women with intact uterus taking concurrent oestrogen.
counselingAdvice: Take at bedtime as it induces drowsiness. Take on an empty stomach (food markedly increases absorption).
cautionsAndContraindications: Contains soya lecithin (avoid in peanut or soya allergy). Contraindicated in severe hepatic dysfunction and unexplained vaginal bleeding.
adverseEffects: Drowsiness, dizziness, headache, bloating, breast tenderness, mood changes.
monitoringAdvice: Annual review of HRT necessity; investigate any abnormal postmenopausal breakthrough bleeding.

name: Slinda (Drospirenone) 4 mg (24 active + 4 placebo tablets) Tablet Pack (28 days)
defaultFrequency: Once daily at the same time
defaultDirections: Take ONE tablet ONCE daily at the same time every day for 28 consecutive days without skipping. 24-hour missed pill window.
indication: Oral contraception in women, including those where oestrogen is contraindicated (smokers >35y, history of VTE, breastfeeding, migraine with aura).
mechanismOfAction: Inhibits ovulation in 97% of cycles, thickens cervical mucus, and suppresses endometrial receptivity.
pbsRestrictionNote: Private prescription in Australia.
counselingAdvice: Take at the same time every day. Unlike traditional minipills, Slinda has a forgiving 24-hour window for missed pills. Unscheduled spotting is common in the first few months.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in severe renal impairment, adrenal insufficiency, and progestogen-dependent tumours.
adverseEffects: Irregular bleeding/spotting, acne, headache, breast tenderness, mood changes.
monitoringAdvice: Assess bleeding pattern and blood pressure.

name: Flomaxtra (Tamsulosin) 400 mcg (0.4 mg) Modified Release Tablet
defaultDirections: Take ONE tablet ONCE daily after breakfast or the first meal of the day. Swallow whole.
indication: Relief of lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) associated with benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) and facilitation of ureteric calculus expulsion.
mechanismOfAction: Selectively and competitively binds to postsynaptic alpha1A-adrenoceptors in the prostate, bladder neck, and prostatic urethra, relaxing smooth muscle and improving urinary flow.
pbsRestrictionNote: Benign prostatic hyperplasia with urinary flow impairment.
warningNote: Intraoperative Floppy Iris Syndrome (IFIS): Inform your cataract surgeon prior to eye surgery. Mild orthostatic dizziness may occur upon standing.
counselingAdvice: Take after breakfast every day. Swallow whole with water; do not crush or chew. Rise slowly from sitting or lying down to prevent dizziness.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in history of orthostatic hypotension and severe hepatic impairment.
adverseEffects: Dizziness, abnormal ejaculation (retrograde ejaculation), headache, asthenia, rhinitis.
monitoringAdvice: Check blood pressure; evaluate urinary flow rate and post-void residual volume.

name: Viagra (Sildenafil) 50 mg Tablet
defaultFrequency: 1 hour prior to sexual activity PRN
defaultDirections: Take ONE tablet approximately 60 minutes before sexual activity. Maximum ONE dose in 24 hours.
indication: Treatment of erectile dysfunction in adult males.
mechanismOfAction: Enhances the effect of nitric oxide by inhibiting PDE5 in the corpus cavernosum, increasing cGMP levels and causing arterial smooth muscle relaxation and erection.
pbsRestrictionNote: Private prescription in Australia.
warningNote: ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATION WITH NITRATES: Never take with glyceryl trinitrate, isosorbide, or recreational amyl nitrite (poppers). Fatal hypotension risk.
counselingAdvice: Take 30-60 minutes before sexual activity. Sexual stimulation is needed for it to work. High-fat meals may delay onset. Seek emergency help if an erection lasts >4 hours (priapism).
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated with all nitrates and riociguat. Caution in recent stroke, MI, severe hypotension, or retinitis pigmentosa.
adverseEffects: Headache, facial flushing, dyspepsia, nasal congestion, blue-tinted visual disturbances (cyanopsia).
monitoringAdvice: Cardiovascular health assessment prior to prescribing.

name: Voltaren Rapid (Diclofenac potassium) 50 mg Tablet
defaultFrequency: Two to three times daily with food
defaultDirections: Take ONE tablet TWO to THREE times daily with food as needed for acute pain (Max 150mg/24h).
indication: Short-term treatment of acute painful inflammatory conditions, musculoskeletal trauma, dental pain, and dysmenorrhoea.
mechanismOfAction: Inhibits both COX-1 and COX-2 enzymes, decreasing synthesis of pro-inflammatory prostaglandins.
pbsRestrictionNote: Acute inflammatory pain.
counselingAdvice: Always take with food or milk to protect your stomach. Stop taking and consult doctor if you experience severe stomach pain or black tarry stools.
cautionsAndContraindications: Avoid in peptic ulcer disease, heart failure, and severe renal impairment. Avoid in 3rd trimester of pregnancy.
adverseEffects: Epigastric pain, nausea, diarrhoea, fluid retention, elevated blood pressure, gastrointestinal ulceration.
monitoringAdvice: Monitor blood pressure and renal function with recurrent use.

name: Elocon (Mometasone furoate) 0.1% Ointment / Cream (45 g)
defaultDirections: Apply a small thin layer to affected skin ONCE daily. Gently massage into skin.
indication: Relief of inflammatory and pruritic manifestations of corticosteroid-responsive dermatoses such as psoriasis and atopic dermatitis.
mechanismOfAction: Binds to intracellular glucocorticoid receptors, down-regulating nuclear factor-kappa B and suppressing inflammatory mediators.
pbsRestrictionNote: Severe corticosteroid-responsive dermatoses.
warningNote: Do not apply to face or flexures. Limit continuous daily application to 2-3 weeks to avoid skin thinning.
counselingAdvice: Apply once a day only (often in the evening). A little goes a long way. Do not apply to open sores, weeping infections, or the face.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in rosacea, acne vulgaris, and viral or fungal skin infections.
adverseEffects: Burning, pruritus, skin atrophy, striae, folliculitis.
monitoringAdvice: Check skin integrity and response to therapy.

name: Differin (Adapalene) 0.1% Gel (30 g)
defaultDirections: Apply a thin film to the entire affected face ONCE daily at bedtime after gentle washing and drying.
indication: Topical treatment of mild to moderate acne vulgaris characterised by comedones, papules, and pustules.
mechanismOfAction: Selectively binds to retinoic acid nuclear receptors RAR-beta and RAR-gamma, normalising follicular follicular epithelial desquamation and reducing microcomedone formation.
pbsRestrictionNote: Private prescription medicine.
warningNote: Avoid during pregnancy. Wear SPF 50+ daily (heightened sensitivity to UV sunburn).
counselingAdvice: Apply a pea-sized amount to the whole face at bedtime, avoiding eyes and lips. Initial dryness and peeling are normal; use a non-comedogenic moisturiser.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in pregnancy and women planning pregnancy. Avoid contact with broken skin, sunburn, and eczema.
adverseEffects: Dry skin, erythema, skin burning sensation, peeling, photosensitivity.
monitoringAdvice: Assess skin tolerability and acne reduction after 8-12 weeks.

name: Cosopt (Dorzolamide + Timolol) 2% / 0.5% Eye Drops (5 mL)
drugClass: Carbonic Anhydrase Inhibitor + Beta-Blocker Eye Drops
defaultDirections: Instil ONE drop into the affected eye(s) TWICE daily morning and night.
indication: Reduction of elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) in patients with open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension insufficiently responsive to beta-blockers alone.
mechanismOfAction: Dorzolamide inhibits carbonic anhydrase II in the ciliary process, decreasing bicarbonate and aqueous humor secretion; timolol reduces aqueous formation via beta-adrenergic blockade.
pbsRestrictionNote: Open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension.
warningNote: Systemic beta-blocker absorption: Contraindicated in bronchial asthma, severe COPD, bradycardia, and high-degree heart block.
counselingAdvice: Compress the tear duct at the inner corner of the eye for 1-2 minutes after drop to reduce systemic absorption into the bloodstream.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in asthma, history of bronchospasm, severe COPD, sinus bradycardia, second- or third-degree AV block, and cardiogenic shock.
adverseEffects: Ocular burning and stinging, bitter taste in mouth, conjunctival injection, blurred vision, bradycardia.
monitoringAdvice: Regular intraocular pressure checks; monitor pulse and respiratory status in vulnerable patients.

name: Contrave (Naltrexone hydrochloride + Bupropion hydrochloride) 8 mg / 90 mg Extended Release Tablet
defaultDose: Titrate from 1 tablet daily to 2 tablets twice daily
defaultDirections: Take with food. Titrate weekly according to dosing schedule: Week 1: 1 tab mane; Week 2: 1 tab mane + 1 tab nocte; Week 4: 2 tabs twice daily.
indication: Adjunct to a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity for chronic weight management in obese (BMI >= 30) or overweight (BMI >= 27) adults with comorbidities.
mechanismOfAction: Bupropion stimulates hypothalamic POMC neurons releasing alpha-MSH and beta-endorphin; naltrexone blocks auto-inhibitory feedback on POMC, sustaining appetite suppression and craving reduction.
pbsRestrictionNote: Private prescription in Australia.
warningNote: Black Box: Neuropsychiatric events and seizure risk (bupropion lowers seizure threshold). Never co-prescribe with opioid analgesics.
counselingAdvice: Swallow tablets whole; do not cut, crush, or chew. Do not take with high-fat meals. Avoid alcohol.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in uncontrolled hypertension, seizure disorder, eating disorders (bulimia/anorexia), and current chronic opioid therapy.
adverseEffects: Nausea, constipation, headache, vomiting, dizziness, insomnia, dry mouth, elevated blood pressure.
monitoringAdvice: Check blood pressure and heart rate every 4 weeks; evaluate weight loss at 16 weeks (discontinue if <5% baseline weight lost).

name: Xenical (Orlistat) 120 mg Capsule
defaultDirections: Take ONE capsule with water immediately before, during, or up to 1 hour after each main meal containing fat.
indication: Management of obesity in conjunction with a mildly hypocaloric, low-fat diet.
mechanismOfAction: Reversibly inhibits gastric and pancreatic lipases in the lumen of the stomach and small intestine, preventing the hydrolysis of dietary triglycerides and blocking absorption of ~30% of ingested fat.
pbsRestrictionNote: OTC / Private prescription in Australia.
counselingAdvice: Take with meals containing fat. If a meal is missed or contains zero fat, the dose can be omitted. Take a daily multivitamin containing fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) at bedtime.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in chronic malabsorption syndrome and cholestasis.
adverseEffects: Oily spotting from rectum, flatus with discharge, fecal urgency, fatty/oily evacuation, increased defecation.
monitoringAdvice: Assess dietary fat intake compliance; check fat-soluble vitamin levels in chronic use.

name: Ferinject (Ferric carboxymaltose) 500 mg / 10 mL Intravenous Infusion Vial
defaultDirections: Administer 500mg to 1000mg by intravenous drip infusion diluted in 0.9% sodium chloride over 15 minutes by healthcare professional.
indication: Treatment of iron deficiency anaemia when oral iron preparations are ineffective, not tolerated, or there is clinical need to deliver iron rapidly.
mechanismOfAction: Iron core surrounded by a carbohydrate shell that releases iron gradually to ferritin and transferrin, replenishing reticuloendothelial iron stores and bone marrow erythropoiesis.
pbsRestrictionNote: Iron deficiency anaemia confirmed by blood tests where oral iron is contraindicated, ineffective, or not tolerated.
warningNote: Extravasation Risk: Can cause permanent brown skin staining. Ensure secure IV access before infusing. Resuscitation equipment must be available.
counselingAdvice: You will be monitored for 30 minutes following the infusion for any allergic reaction. Mild headache or temporary joint ache can occur over the next 24-48 hours.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in iron overload (hemochromatosis), hypersensitivity to IV iron, and first trimester of pregnancy.
adverseEffects: Transient hypophosphataemia, flushing, headache, nausea, hypertension, injection site skin staining.
monitoringAdvice: Serum ferritin and full blood count 4 to 8 weeks post-infusion; monitor serum phosphate.

name: Lokelma (Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate) 10 g Powder for Oral Suspension Sachet (30 sachets)
form: Powder for Oral Suspension Sachet (30 sachets)
defaultDirections: Empty packet into a glass, add 45 mL of water, stir well and drink immediately ONCE daily.
indication: Treatment of hyperkalaemia in adult patients, enabling continuation of cardio-renal protective RAAS inhibitor therapy.
mechanismOfAction: Inorganic, non-absorbed crystal lattice with uniform micropores that preferentially entrap potassium cations throughout the GI tract in exchange for sodium and hydrogen.
pbsRestrictionNote: Hyperkalaemia in patients with chronic kidney disease or heart failure.
counselingAdvice: Stir powder in water and drink while cloudy. Space all other oral medicines by at least 2 hours before or 2 hours after Lokelma.
cautionsAndContraindications: Caution in patients with severe constipation or bowel impaction.
adverseEffects: Hypokalaemia, constipation, peripheral oedema (due to sodium load).
monitoringAdvice: Regular serum potassium monitoring; check for signs of volume overload.

name: Augmentin Duo Forte (amoxicillin 875mg + clavulanic acid 125mg tablet)
indication: Treatment of bacterial infections including sinusitis, community-acquired pneumonia, acute exacerbation of COPD, and bite wounds.
mechanismOfAction: Amoxicillin inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis; clavulanate inactivates beta-lactamase enzymes to broaden antibacterial spectrum.
pbsRestrictionNote: Restricted Benefit: Severe bacterial infections resistant to amoxicillin alone.
counselingAdvice: Take at the start of a meal or with a light snack to minimise gastrointestinal intolerance. Complete the full prescribed course.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in patients with severe penicillin allergy or prior amoxicillin/clavulanate-associated jaundice or hepatic impairment.
adverseEffects: Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, candidiasis, rash, elevated transaminases.
monitoringAdvice: Assess resolution of infection symptoms. Monitor hepatic function in prolonged courses.
storageAdvice: Store below 25°C in a dry place. Protect from moisture.
defaultDirections: Take 1 tablet twice daily with food for 5 to 7 days.

commonDoses.label: Standard course (5 days)
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet every 12 hours with food for 5 days.

commonDoses.label: Extended course (7 days)
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet every 12 hours with food for 7 days.

warningNote: Ensure patient is not anaphylactic to penicillins or beta-lactams.

name: Minomycin (minocycline 100mg capsule)
indication: Treatment of moderate to severe acne vulgaris and susceptible bacterial infections.
mechanismOfAction: Reversibly binds to 30S ribosomal subunits inhibiting bacterial protein synthesis; possesses anti-inflammatory properties.
pbsRestrictionNote: Restricted benefit for severe inflammatory acne.
counselingAdvice: Take with a full glass of water and remain upright for 30 minutes to prevent oesophageal irritation. Avoid taking with antacids, iron, or dairy products.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children under 8 years due to risk of permanent tooth discolouration and enamel hypoplasia.
adverseEffects: Dizziness, lightheadedness, photosensitivity, benign intracranial hypertension, blue-grey skin/mucosal pigmentation on prolonged therapy.
monitoringAdvice: Monitor liver function, renal function, and signs of autoimmune disorders (lupus-like syndrome) with long-term therapy.
storageAdvice: Store below 30°C in a cool, dry place.
defaultDirections: Take 1 capsule daily with a large glass of water. Do not lie down for 30 minutes after taking.

commonDoses.label: Acne maintenance
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 capsule once daily with meals and water.

commonDoses.label: Acute infection
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 capsule twice daily for 7-10 days.

warningNote: Contraindicated in pregnancy (Category D - fetal tooth and bone toxicity).

name: Eryc (erythromycin 250mg delayed-release capsule)
indication: Infections caused by susceptible organisms, alternative in penicillin-allergic patients; acne vulgaris, legionella, campylobacter.
mechanismOfAction: Binds reversibly to the 50S ribosomal subunit of susceptible microorganisms, inhibiting protein synthesis.
counselingAdvice: Take on an empty stomach with a full glass of water 1 hour before or 2 hours after meals. If gastrointestinal upset occurs, take with food.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated with simvastatin, atorvastatin, and other strong CYP3A4 substrates, or medications causing QT prolongation.
adverseEffects: Nausea, vomiting, abdominal cramps, diarrhoea, QT prolongation, ototoxicity (high doses).
monitoringAdvice: Monitor for GI tolerance and cardiac rhythm in patients at risk of arrhythmias.
defaultDirections: Take 1 to 2 capsules four times daily, preferably 1 hour before meals.

commonDoses.label: Standard 250mg QDS
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 capsule every 6 hours for 5 to 7 days.

commonDoses.label: Severe 500mg QDS
commonDoses.directions: Take 2 capsules every 6 hours for 7 days.

warningNote: Potent CYP3A4 inhibitor - check concurrent statins and antiarrhythmics.

name: Ciproxin (ciprofloxacin 500mg tablet)
indication: Complicated urinary tract infections, pyelonephritis, pseudomonal infections, severe gastroenteritis, bone and joint infections.
mechanismOfAction: Inhibits bacterial DNA topoisomerase II (DNA gyrase) and topoisomerase IV, preventing DNA replication and repair.
pbsRestrictionNote: Restricted Benefit: Bacterial infections resistant to other oral agents, or severe Gram-negative infections.
counselingAdvice: Drink plenty of water while taking this medicine. Avoid antacids, dairy, iron, or zinc within 2 hours of dosing. Stop and report tendon pain immediately.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated with history of tendon disorders related to fluoroquinolones, or concurrent tizanidine. Use with caution in elderly, myasthenia gravis, or prolonged QT.
adverseEffects: Tendinitis, tendon rupture, QT prolongation, peripheral neuropathy, nausea, diarrhoea, headache, insomnia, photosensitivity.
monitoringAdvice: Monitor renal function, signs of tendinopathy, and CNS symptoms.
defaultDirections: Take 1 tablet every 12 hours with plenty of fluids for 5 to 7 days.

commonDoses.label: Complicated UTI (500mg BD)
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet every 12 hours for 7 days.

commonDoses.label: Severe systemic infection (750mg BD)
commonDoses.directions: Take 1.5 tablets every 12 hours for 10-14 days.

warningNote: Black box warning for tendinitis, tendon rupture, and peripheral neuropathy.

name: Klacid (clarithromycin 500mg tablet)
indication: Lower and upper respiratory tract infections, skin infections, Helicobacter pylori eradication (in combination with PPI and amoxicillin).
mechanismOfAction: Reversibly binds to the 50S ribosomal subunit of susceptible organisms, inhibiting bacterial protein synthesis.
counselingAdvice: Take with or without food. Complete the full prescribed course. May cause a temporary metallic or bitter taste.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated with statins (atorvastatin, simvastatin), colchicine in renal impairment, or drugs causing QT prolongation.
adverseEffects: Taste disturbance (dysgeusia), nausea, diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal pain, headache, transaminase elevation, QT prolongation.
monitoringAdvice: Assess response to treatment. Review drug interaction profile carefully.
defaultDirections: Take 1 tablet twice daily with food for 7 to 14 days.

commonDoses.label: Respiratory infection
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet every 12 hours with meals for 7 days.

commonDoses.label: H. pylori eradication
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet twice daily with Nexium and Amoxil for 7 days.

warningNote: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitor - hold concurrent simvastatin/atorvastatin.

name: Macrodantin (nitrofurantoin 50mg capsule)
indication: Acute uncomplicated cystitis; prophylaxis against recurrent urinary tract infections.
mechanismOfAction: Inactivated by bacterial nitroreductases into reactive intermediates that attack bacterial ribosomal proteins, DNA, and metabolic enzymes.
counselingAdvice: Take with meals or milk to improve absorption and avoid stomach upset. May colour the urine brown; this is harmless.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30 mL/min), G6PD deficiency, and at term in pregnancy (weeks 38-42) due to risk of neonatal haemolytic anaemia.
adverseEffects: Nausea, anorexia, dark urine, peripheral neuropathy, acute/chronic pulmonary fibrosis with prolonged use.
monitoringAdvice: Check renal function. With prolonged prophylaxis (> 6 months), monitor pulmonary symptoms and liver function.
defaultDirections: Take 1 to 2 capsules four times daily with food for 5 days.

commonDoses.label: Acute cystitis (50mg QDS)
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 capsule with food 4 times daily for 5 days.

commonDoses.label: Recurrent UTI prevention (50mg nocte)
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 capsule at bedtime every night.

warningNote: Contraindicated if eGFR < 30 mL/min (ineffective in bladder and increases neurotoxicity risk).

name: Alprim (trimethoprim 300mg tablet)
indication: First-line empirical treatment of acute uncomplicated urinary tract infections in women and men.
mechanismOfAction: Selectively inhibits bacterial dihydrofolate reductase, blocking conversion of dihydrofolic acid to tetrahydrofolic acid.
counselingAdvice: Take once daily at bedtime with a full glass of water. Complete the 3 to 7 day course.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in severe renal failure (eGFR < 15 mL/min), megaloblastic anaemia secondary to folate deficiency, or first trimester of pregnancy.
adverseEffects: Nausea, pruritus, rash, hyperkalaemia, mild elevation in serum creatinine due to competitive tubular secretion inhibition.
monitoringAdvice: Check potassium levels if co-prescribed with ACE inhibitors, ARBs, or spironolactone.
defaultDirections: Take 1 tablet once daily at bedtime for 3 days (females) or 7 days (males).

commonDoses.label: Female uncomplicated cystitis (3 days)
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet nightly for 3 days.

commonDoses.label: Male / complicated UTI (7 days)
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet nightly for 7 days.

warningNote: Avoid during the first trimester of pregnancy (folate antagonist).

name: Bactrim DS (sulfamethoxazole 800mg + trimethoprim 160mg tablet)
indication: Treatment and prophylaxis of Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia, shigellosis, melioidosis, MRSA skin infections.
mechanismOfAction: Synergistic sequential blockade of bacterial folic acid synthesis (sulfamethoxazole inhibits dihydropteroate synthase; trimethoprim inhibits dihydrofolate reductase).
counselingAdvice: Drink plenty of water to prevent crystalluria. Discontinue and seek urgent medical attention if rash or skin peeling occurs.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in severe sulfonamide allergy, megaloblastic anaemia, severe hepatic or renal impairment, or pregnancy at term.
adverseEffects: Nausea, vomiting, hypersensitivity rash, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, hyperkalaemia, bone marrow suppression, haemolysis in G6PD deficiency.
monitoringAdvice: Full blood count, serum potassium, and renal function on extended therapy.
storageAdvice: Store below 30°C in a dry place.
defaultDirections: Take 1 tablet twice daily with food and abundant fluid.

commonDoses.label: Standard infection
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet every 12 hours for 5 to 7 days.

commonDoses.label: PJP Prophylaxis
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet on Monday, Wednesday, Friday.

warningNote: Severe risk of Stevens-Johnson syndrome in sulfonamide-sensitive patients.

name: Famvir (famciclovir 500mg tablet)
indication: Treatment of herpes zoster (shingles), genital herpes simplex episodes, and suppression of recurrent genital herpes.
mechanismOfAction: Prodrug of penciclovir; selectively phosphorylated by viral thymidine kinase, competitively inhibiting viral DNA polymerase.
pbsRestrictionNote: Authority Required: Acute herpes zoster within 72 hours of rash onset, or immunocompromised patients.
counselingAdvice: Initiate as soon as possible after symptom onset (within 72 hours of rash for shingles). Drink plenty of fluids.
cautionsAndContraindications: Reduce dosage in renal impairment based on creatinine clearance.
adverseEffects: Headache, nausea, diarrhoea, fatigue, dizziness.
monitoringAdvice: Assess clinical resolution of herpetic lesions and renal function.
defaultDirections: Take 1 tablet three times daily (every 8 hours) for 7 days.

commonDoses.label: Herpes Zoster (Shingles)
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet every 8 hours for 7 days.

commonDoses.label: Genital Herpes First Episode
commonDoses.directions: Take 250mg three times daily for 5 days.

commonDoses.label: Recurrent Cold Sores
commonDoses.directions: Take 3 tablets (1500mg) as a single dose at earliest tingling.

warningNote: Start within 72 hours of shingles rash for optimal neuropathic pain prevention.

name: Valtrex (valaciclovir 500mg tablet)
indication: Treatment of herpes zoster (shingles), cold sores (herpes labialis), genital herpes treatment and chronic suppression.
mechanismOfAction: L-valyl ester prodrug of aciclovir; rapidly converted in vivo and inhibits viral DNA synthesis.
pbsRestrictionNote: Authority Required: Herpes zoster treated within 72 hours of onset.
counselingAdvice: Take with or without food. Maintain adequate hydration during treatment.
cautionsAndContraindications: Dose reduction mandatory in renal impairment to prevent neurotoxicity.
adverseEffects: Headache, nausea, abdominal discomfort, dizziness, confusion (in elderly with renal insufficiency).
monitoringAdvice: Hydration status and renal function.
defaultDirections: Take 2 tablets (1000mg) three times daily for 7 days for shingles.

commonDoses.label: Shingles (1000mg TDS)
commonDoses.directions: Take 2 tablets every 8 hours for 7 days.

commonDoses.label: Cold Sore (2000mg BD x 1 day)
commonDoses.directions: Take 4 tablets at onset, then 4 tablets 12h later.

commonDoses.label: Suppression of Genital Herpes
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet once daily continuously.

warningNote: Adjust dosage in patients with renal impairment to avoid neurotoxicity.

name: Diflucan (fluconazole 150mg capsule)
indication: Vaginal candidiasis (thrush), mucosal candidiasis, invasive candidiasis, cryptococcal meningitis.
mechanismOfAction: Inhibits fungal cytochrome P450-dependent enzyme lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase, disrupting ergosterol synthesis in fungal cell membranes.
counselingAdvice: Take capsule whole with a glass of water, with or without food. Symptoms typically improve within 24 to 48 hours.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in pregnancy (Category D: associated with congenital malformations with high/prolonged doses). Caution with QT-prolonging drugs.
adverseEffects: Headache, nausea, abdominal pain, diarrhoea, transient elevation of liver enzymes, rash.
monitoringAdvice: Liver function in recurrent or prolonged therapy.
defaultDirections: Take 1 capsule (150mg) as a single oral dose.

commonDoses.label: Vaginal thrush single dose
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 capsule as a single dose.

commonDoses.label: Recurrent candidiasis pulse
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 capsule once weekly for 6 months as directed.

warningNote: Avoid during pregnancy - high dose or first trimester exposure linked to birth defects.

name: Lumigan (bimatoprost 0.01% eye drops 3mL)
indication: Reduction of elevated intraocular pressure in open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension.
mechanismOfAction: Mimics endogenous prostamides to increase trabecular meshwork and uveoscleral outflow of aqueous humour.
pbsRestrictionNote: Restricted Benefit: Reduction of elevated intraocular pressure in patients with glaucoma or ocular hypertension.
counselingAdvice: Instil 1 drop into the affected eye(s) once daily in the evening. Remove contact lenses prior to application and wait 15 minutes before reinserting. May cause gradual darkening of the iris and eyelash growth.
cautionsAndContraindications: Caution in active intraocular inflammation (uveitis, iritis) or macular oedema.
adverseEffects: Conjunctival hyperaemia, eyelash darkening/thickening, iris hyperpigmentation (permanent), periocular skin darkening, ocular irritation.
monitoringAdvice: Monitor intraocular pressure regularly; inspect iris and periocular skin.
storageAdvice: Store below 25°C. Discard 4 weeks after opening.
defaultDirections: Instil 1 drop into the affected eye(s) once daily in the evening.

commonDoses.label: Standard daily evening dose
commonDoses.directions: Instil 1 drop into each affected eye every night.

warningNote: May cause permanent brown pigmentation of the iris and increased eyelash growth.

name: Travatan (travoprost 0.004% eye drops 2.5mL)
indication: Reduction of elevated intraocular pressure in open-angle glaucoma and ocular hypertension.
mechanismOfAction: Prostaglandin FP receptor agonist that increases uveoscleral outflow of aqueous humor.
counselingAdvice: Instil 1 drop once daily in the evening. Press finger against tear duct (nasolacrimal occlusion) for 1 minute after instillation to minimise systemic absorption.
cautionsAndContraindications: Avoid in patients with severe uveitis or aphakic patients predisposed to macular oedema.
adverseEffects: Ocular hyperaemia, blurred vision, iris pigmentation, eyelash elongation, dry eye sensations.
monitoringAdvice: Check intraocular pressure every 3 to 6 months.
storageAdvice: Store below 25°C. Discard 4 weeks after breaking seal.
defaultDirections: Instil 1 drop into the affected eye(s) once daily at bedtime.

commonDoses.label: Standard nocte drop
commonDoses.directions: Instil 1 drop in affected eye(s) every evening.

name: Alphagan (brimonidine tartrate 0.2% eye drops 5mL)
indication: Lowering intraocular pressure in patients with chronic open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension.
mechanismOfAction: Selective alpha-2 adrenergic agonist; reduces aqueous humour production and stimulates uveoscleral outflow.
counselingAdvice: Instil 1 drop into the affected eye(s) twice daily, approximately 12 hours apart. May cause drowsiness or dry mouth.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in neonates and infants under 2 years (causes severe CNS depression and hypotension). Contraindicated with MAO inhibitors.
adverseEffects: Ocular allergic reactions (conjunctival blanching, folliculosis), oral dryness, somnolence, fatigue, headache, dizziness.
monitoringAdvice: Monitor intraocular pressure and watch for delayed allergic conjunctivitis.
defaultDirections: Instil 1 drop into the affected eye(s) twice daily (approx 12 hours apart).

commonDoses.label: Twice daily standard
commonDoses.directions: Instil 1 drop twice daily 12 hours apart.

warningNote: Contraindicated in infants and children under 2 years due to life-threatening CNS depression.

name: Maxidex (dexamethasone 0.1% ophthalmic suspension 5mL)
indication: Non-infectious inflammatory conditions of the eye including anterior uveitis, episcleritis, and post-operative inflammation.
mechanismOfAction: Potent corticosteroid that suppresses inflammatory cytokine release, reduces vascular permeability and leucocyte migration in ocular tissue.
counselingAdvice: Shake bottle well before use. Do not touch dropper tip to eye or skin. Taper dose gradually as instructed by clinician.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in active viral diseases of the cornea (e.g., herpes simplex keratitis), fungal or mycobacterial eye infections.
adverseEffects: Elevated intraocular pressure (steroid glaucoma), posterior subcapsular cataract formation, secondary infection, delayed corneal healing.
monitoringAdvice: Monitor intraocular pressure regularly if therapy extends beyond 10 days.
storageAdvice: Store upright below 25°C. Do not freeze.
defaultDirections: Shake well. Instil 1 drop into the affected eye(s) every 4 to 6 hours as directed.

commonDoses.label: Acute uveitis (QDS)
commonDoses.directions: Instil 1 drop four times daily, tapering over 2-4 weeks.

commonDoses.label: Intensive starter
commonDoses.directions: Instil 1 drop every 2 hours for 48 hours, then reduce to QDS.

warningNote: Must exclude herpes simplex dendritic keratitis before prescribing ocular steroids.

name: Sofradex (framycetin + gramicidin + dexamethasone ear/eye drops 8mL)
indication: Otitis externa with intact tympanic membrane; anterior ocular inflammation with superficial bacterial infection.
mechanismOfAction: Broad-spectrum antibacterial action (framycetin against gram-negatives, gramicidin against gram-positives) combined with dexamethasone anti-inflammatory action.
counselingAdvice: Lie with affected ear uppermost for 2 minutes after instilling drops. Warm the bottle in hands before instillation to prevent vertigo.
cautionsAndContraindications: Strictly contraindicated if the tympanic membrane is perforated or patent grommets are present due to aminoglycoside ototoxicity (sensorineural deafness).
adverseEffects: Local stinging, transient burning, contact dermatitis, irreversible ototoxicity if enters middle ear.
monitoringAdvice: Otoscopic examination to confirm intact eardrum prior to initiation.
defaultDirections: Instil 2 to 3 drops into the affected ear(s) 3 to 4 times daily for up to 7 days.

commonDoses.label: Otitis externa (TDS)
commonDoses.directions: Instil 3 drops into the ear canal 3 times daily for 7 days.

warningNote: CONTRAINDICATED if eardrum is perforated — high risk of irreversible ototoxicity.

name: Otocomb Otic / Kenacomb (triamcinolone + neomycin + gramicidin + nystatin ear drops 7.5mL)
drugClass: Combination Steroid, Antibacterial, and Antifungal Ear Preparation
indication: Otitis externa complicated by fungal co-infection (otomycosis) or eczema of the external auditory meatus.
mechanismOfAction: Triamcinolone reduces swelling and pruritus; neomycin and gramicidin treat mixed bacterial flora; nystatin eradicates Candida fungal species.
counselingAdvice: Instil into the ear canal after clearing debris. Do not use for more than 7 consecutive days without medical review.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in tympanic membrane perforation (neomycin ototoxicity) and viral ear canal infections (herpes zoster oticus).
adverseEffects: Local irritation, allergic contact dermatitis, ototoxicity if middle ear breached.
monitoringAdvice: Check tympanic membrane integrity with otoscope.
storageAdvice: Store at 2°C to 8°C (Refrigerate). Do not freeze.
defaultDirections: Instil 2 to 3 drops into the affected ear canal twice or three times daily for 7 days.

commonDoses.label: Standard otic instillation
commonDoses.directions: Instil 3 drops into ear canal morning and evening for 7 days.

warningNote: Verify tympanic membrane is intact before prescribing; store in refrigerator.

name: Roaccutane / Oratane (isotretinoin 20mg capsule)
indication: Severe cystic or conglobate acne resistant to adequate courses of conventional systemic antibacterials.
mechanismOfAction: Induces sebaceous gland atrophy, markedly suppresses sebum secretion, reduces follicular keratinisation and Cutibacterium acnes colonization.
pbsRestrictionNote: Authority Required: Severe cystic acne unresponsive to conventional oral therapies, initiated or endorsed by dermatologist.
counselingAdvice: Extremely teratogenic. Strict pregnancy prevention mandatory before, during, and for 1 month after therapy. Take with a fatty meal for optimal absorption. Apply lip balm regularly.
cautionsAndContraindications: Strictly contraindicated in pregnancy or women planning pregnancy. Contraindicated with vitamin A supplements or tetracyclines (risk of pseudotumor cerebri).
adverseEffects: Cheilitis (nearly 100%), xerosis, epistaxis, conjunctivitis, hypertriglyceridaemia, transaminitis, mood changes, arthralgia.
monitoringAdvice: Mandatory monthly pregnancy testing for females of childbearing potential. Baseline and periodic fasting lipids, LFTs, and full blood count.
storageAdvice: Store below 25°C. Protect from light and moisture.
defaultDirections: Take 1 capsule (20mg) once daily with dinner or fatty meal.

commonDoses.label: Low-dose / Initiation (20mg daily)
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 capsule daily with dinner.

commonDoses.label: Full weight-based (40mg daily)
commonDoses.directions: Take 2 capsules (40mg) daily with main meal.

warningNote: CATEGORY X: Extreme risk of severe fetal malformations. Requires strict contraception.

name: Epiduo (adapalene 0.1% + benzoyl peroxide 2.5% gel 50g)
indication: Topical treatment of acne vulgaris with comedones, papules, and pustules.
mechanismOfAction: Adapalene normalises follicular epithelial differentiation and reduces inflammation; benzoyl peroxide is bactericidal against Cutibacterium acnes with keratolytic activity.
counselingAdvice: Apply a pea-sized amount to the entire clean, dry face at night. Avoid eyes, lips, and mucous membranes. Will bleach coloured towels, clothing, and hair. Use daily broad-spectrum sunscreen.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in pregnancy or planning pregnancy. Avoid concomitant peeling agents.
adverseEffects: Erythema, scaling, skin dryness, burning/stinging sensation, contact dermatitis, photosensitivity.
monitoringAdvice: Assess tolerance at 4 weeks; reduce to alternate night application if severe peeling occurs.
defaultDirections: Apply a thin layer over clean, dry facial skin once daily at bedtime. Wash hands thoroughly.

commonDoses.label: Nightly application
commonDoses.directions: Apply thin layer to face at night after gentle cleanser.

commonDoses.label: Sensitive skin (Alternate nights)
commonDoses.directions: Apply alternate nights for 2 weeks, then nightly if tolerated.

warningNote: Bleaches hair and coloured fabrics; contraindicated in pregnancy.

name: Soolantra (ivermectin 10mg/g / 1% cream 30g)
indication: Topical treatment of inflammatory lesions of papulopustular rosacea in adult patients.
mechanismOfAction: Causes death of Demodex mites (which play a role in rosacea inflammation) and suppresses pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1b, TNF-a).
pbsRestrictionNote: Restricted Benefit: Papulopustular rosacea unresponsive to other topical therapies.
counselingAdvice: Apply a pea-sized amount to forehead, chin, nose, and each cheek once daily at bedtime. Avoid eye area.
cautionsAndContraindications: Hypersensitivity to ivermectin or any excipient.
adverseEffects: Skin burning sensation, pruritus, skin irritation, dry skin.
monitoringAdvice: Evaluate clinical response after 8 to 12 weeks of continuous treatment.
defaultDose: Pea-sized amount to affected facial areas
defaultDirections: Apply a small pea-sized amount to each of the 5 areas of the face once daily at bedtime.

commonDoses.label: Once daily bedtime course
commonDoses.directions: Apply thinly over forehead, nose, cheeks, and chin at bedtime.

name: Rozex (metronidazole 0.75% gel / cream 30g)
indication: Topical treatment of inflammatory papules, pustules, and erythema of rosacea.
mechanismOfAction: Exerts anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial effects by reducing reactive oxygen species.
counselingAdvice: Cleanse skin with mild non-soap cleanser and let dry before applying. Apply thinly twice daily.
cautionsAndContraindications: Known hypersensitivity to metronidazole.
adverseEffects: Mild skin burning, irritation, dryness, contact dermatitis, lacrimation if applied near eyes.
monitoringAdvice: Review skin lesions at 6 to 9 weeks.
defaultDirections: Apply a thin film to affected areas of face twice daily, morning and evening.

commonDoses.label: Standard BD application
commonDoses.directions: Apply thinly over affected facial skin twice daily.

name: Advantan (methylprednisolone aceponate 0.1% fatty ointment / cream 15g)
indication: Atopic dermatitis (eczema), neurodermatitis, contact eczema, nummular eczema.
mechanismOfAction: High-affinity binding to glucocorticoid receptors in the skin; undergoes bioactivation in inflamed epidermis with low systemic absorption.
counselingAdvice: Apply thinly once daily to affected skin only. Wash hands after use. Avoid prolonged use on the face, groin, or axillae.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in untreated bacterial, fungal, or tuberculous skin infections; perioral dermatitis, rosacea.
adverseEffects: Skin atrophy, telangiectasia, striae, folliculitis, perioral dermatitis with prolonged facial use.
monitoringAdvice: Limit continuous application to 12 weeks in adults, 4 weeks in children.
defaultDirections: Apply sparingly to affected areas once daily until clinical improvement occurs.

commonDoses.label: Standard once daily flare control
