commonDoses.directions: Apply thinly once daily to affected eczema patches.

name: Diprosone (betamethasone dipropionate 0.05% cream / ointment 50g)
indication: Relief of inflammatory and pruritic manifestations of corticosteroid-responsive dermatoses, including plaque psoriasis and severe eczema.
mechanismOfAction: Inhibits phospholipase A2, reduces formation of prostaglandins and leukotrienes, suppresses cellular inflammatory infiltration.
counselingAdvice: Apply sparingly once or twice daily. Do not occlude unless directed. Discontinue once flare resolves.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in rosacea, acne, perioral dermatitis, extensive plaque psoriasis, untreated fungal or viral lesions.
adverseEffects: Skin thinning, striae distensae, hypopigmentation, secondary infection, hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis suppression with extensive use.
monitoringAdvice: Do not exceed 50g per week to minimise risk of systemic absorption.
defaultDirections: Apply sparingly to affected areas once or twice daily for up to 2 to 4 weeks.

commonDoses.label: Twice daily flare control
commonDoses.directions: Apply a thin layer to affected skin morning and night.

name: Daivobet (calcipotriol 50mcg/g + betamethasone dipropionate 0.5mg/g ointment / gel 60g)
drugClass: Vitamin D3 Analogue and Potent Corticosteroid
indication: Topical treatment of chronic plaque psoriasis vulgaris on the body or scalp.
mechanismOfAction: Calcipotriol induces differentiation and suppresses proliferation of keratinocytes; betamethasone reduces inflammation, erythema, and pruritus synergistically.
pbsRestrictionNote: Restricted Benefit: Plaque psoriasis.
counselingAdvice: Apply once daily to psoriatic plaques. Wash hands thoroughly after application. Maximum weekly dosage is 100g. Do not apply to face or flexures.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in patients with calcium metabolism disorders, severe renal or hepatic impairment, erythrodermic or pustular psoriasis.
adverseEffects: Pruritus, skin irritation, folliculitis, hypercalcaemia (with overdose > 100g/week), skin atrophy.
monitoringAdvice: Monitor serum calcium if approaching maximum weekly dose (100g/week).
defaultDirections: Apply to affected psoriatic plaques once daily. Maximum 100g per week.

commonDoses.label: Daily application (4 weeks)
commonDoses.directions: Apply once daily to plaques for up to 4 weeks.

warningNote: Do not exceed 100g per week due to risk of systemic hypercalcaemia.

name: Eliquis (apixaban 5mg tablet)
drugClass: Direct Oral Anticoagulant (DOAC) / Factor Xa Inhibitor
indication: Prevention of stroke and systemic embolism in non-valvular atrial fibrillation; treatment and secondary prevention of DVT and PE.
mechanismOfAction: Potent, reversible, direct, and highly selective factor Xa inhibitor that inhibits free and clot-bound factor Xa and prothrombinase activity.
pbsRestrictionNote: Authority Required: Non-valvular atrial fibrillation with >= 1 risk factor, or venous thromboembolism.
counselingAdvice: Take one tablet twice daily with or without food. Do not skip doses. Report any unexplained bleeding, bruising, or black stools promptly.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in clinically significant active bleeding, lesion or condition at significant risk of major bleed, or severe hepatic disease.
adverseEffects: Epistaxis, haematoma, gastrointestinal haemorrhage, haematuria, anaemia, nausea.
monitoringAdvice: Assess renal function (creatinine clearance) at least annually (every 3-6 months if eGFR 30-50 mL/min). Dose reduce to 2.5mg BD if at least 2 of: age >= 80, weight <= 60kg, serum creatinine >= 133 umol/L.
defaultDirections: Take 1 tablet twice daily with water.

commonDoses.label: Standard AF dose (5mg BD)
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet twice daily with or without food.

commonDoses.label: Dose reduction (2.5mg BD criteria met)
commonDoses.directions: Take 2.5mg twice daily if >= 2 of: age >=80, wt <=60kg, Cr >=133.

commonDoses.label: Acute DVT/PE loading (10mg BD x 7d)
commonDoses.directions: Take 2 tablets (10mg) twice daily for 7 days, then 5mg BD.

warningNote: Reduce dose to 2.5mg BD if patient meets 2 or more: age >= 80, wt <= 60kg, Cr >= 133 umol/L.

name: Xarelto (rivaroxaban 20mg tablet)
drugClass: Direct Oral Anticoagulant (DOAC) / Factor Xa Inhibitor
indication: Prevention of stroke in non-valvular atrial fibrillation; treatment of DVT and pulmonary embolism and prevention of recurrent VTE.
mechanismOfAction: Direct, selective, reversible inhibitor of factor Xa, interrupting the intrinsic and extrinsic pathways of the blood coagulation cascade.
pbsRestrictionNote: Authority Required: Non-valvular atrial fibrillation or treatment/prevention of DVT/PE.
counselingAdvice: MUST BE TAKEN WITH FOOD (dinner or main meal) to ensure proper systemic absorption. Report unusual bleeding immediately.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in active major bleeding, hepatic disease with coagulopathy, severe renal impairment (CrCl < 15 mL/min).
adverseEffects: Bleeding, anaemia, dizziness, headache, peripheral oedema, transaminase elevation.
monitoringAdvice: Baseline and regular renal function monitoring. Reduce to 15mg daily if CrCl is 15-49 mL/min.
defaultDirections: Take 1 tablet once daily with the evening meal.

commonDoses.label: Standard AF / DVT maintenance (20mg daily)
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet once daily with the main evening meal.

commonDoses.label: Renal impairment dose (15mg daily with food)
commonDoses.directions: Take 15mg once daily with food if CrCl 15-49 mL/min.

warningNote: MUST be taken with food (absorption drops by 34% if taken on empty stomach).

name: Pradaxa (dabigatran etexilate 150mg capsule)
indication: Prevention of stroke and systemic embolism in patients with non-valvular AF; treatment and secondary prevention of DVT and PE.
mechanismOfAction: Prodrug rapidly hydrolysed to dabigatran, a competitive, reversible, direct thrombin (factor IIa) inhibitor.
counselingAdvice: Swallow whole with a full glass of water. DO NOT OPEN OR CHEW CAPSULES (increases bioavailability by 75% and bleeding risk). Store in original foil blister pack.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in mechanical prosthetic heart valves, severe renal failure (CrCl < 30 mL/min), or active bleeding.
adverseEffects: Dyspepsia, gastritis-like symptoms, gastrointestinal haemorrhage, epistaxis, anaemia.
monitoringAdvice: Assess renal function carefully (dabigatran is 80% renally excreted). Specific reversal agent available (idarucizumab).
storageAdvice: Store below 25°C in the original blister package to protect from moisture. Do not put in dosette boxes.
defaultDirections: Take 1 capsule twice daily with a full glass of water. Swallow whole.

commonDoses.label: Standard AF / VTE (150mg BD)
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 capsule twice daily with water. Do not open capsule.

commonDoses.label: Elderly >= 75 / Bleeding risk (110mg BD)
commonDoses.directions: Take 110mg twice daily if age >= 75 or moderate renal impairment.

warningNote: Do NOT open capsules or dispense in dosette boxes; 80% renally cleared.

name: Brilinta (ticagrelor 90mg tablet)
indication: Prevention of atherothrombotic events in adult patients with acute coronary syndrome (STEMI, NSTEMI, or unstable angina) in combination with aspirin.
mechanismOfAction: Direct, reversibly binding P2Y12 adenosine diphosphate (ADP) receptor antagonist that prevents ADP-mediated platelet activation and aggregation.
pbsRestrictionNote: Authority Required: Acute coronary syndrome treated medically or with PCI.
counselingAdvice: Take one tablet twice daily with or without food, along with low-dose aspirin as directed. Do not stop without cardiologist consultation. Dyspnea may occur but often resolves.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in active pathological bleeding, history of intracranial haemorrhage, severe hepatic impairment, or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors/inducers.
adverseEffects: Dyspnoea, epistaxis, bruising, gastrointestinal haemorrhage, hyperuricaemia, ventricular pauses / bradycardia.
monitoringAdvice: Monitor for symptoms of bleeding and dyspnoea. Assess renal function and uric acid levels.
defaultDirections: Take 1 tablet twice daily with or without food. Co-administer with aspirin 100mg daily.

commonDoses.label: ACS Dual Antiplatelet Therapy
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet twice daily for up to 12 months after ACS.

warningNote: Reversible P2Y12 inhibitor; sudden cessation elevates stent thrombosis risk.

name: Plavix / Iscover (clopidogrel 75mg tablet)
indication: Prevention of vascular ischaemic events in patients with prior myocardial infarction, ischaemic stroke, or established peripheral arterial disease.
mechanismOfAction: Prodrug activated by CYP2C19 to active metabolite that irreversibly inhibits ADP binding to its platelet P2Y12 receptor.
counselingAdvice: Take once daily with or without food. Inform dentists and surgeons that you take clopidogrel prior to procedures.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in active bleeding (peptic ulcer or intracranial haemorrhage). Avoid concurrent omeprazole or esomeprazole (inhibits CYP2C19 activation; use pantoprazole instead).
adverseEffects: Bruising, haematoma, epistaxis, gastrointestinal bleeding, purpura, rash.
monitoringAdvice: Full blood count if purpura or unexplained fever occurs (TTP risk).
defaultDirections: Take 1 tablet once daily with water.

commonDoses.label: Secondary stroke / vascular prevention
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet once daily continuously.

commonDoses.label: DAPT after coronary stent
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet once daily with aspirin 100mg daily for 6-12 months.

warningNote: Avoid combining with omeprazole (inhibits CYP2C19 bioactivation); use pantoprazole.

name: Anginine (glyceryl trinitrate 600mcg sublingual tablet)
indication: Treatment and acute prophylaxis of angina pectoris attacks.
mechanismOfAction: Converted to nitric oxide which stimulates cGMP production, relaxing vascular smooth muscle with predominantly venous pooling and decreased myocardial oxygen demand.
counselingAdvice: Dissolve under the tongue at first onset of chest pain. Sit down before taking to prevent fainting. If pain persists after 2 tablets 5 minutes apart, call 000 immediately.
cautionsAndContraindications: Strictly contraindicated with PDE5 inhibitors (sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil) due to catastrophic fatal hypotension.
adverseEffects: Throbbing headache, flushing, postural hypotension, reflex tachycardia, dizziness.
monitoringAdvice: Instruct on chest pain action plan and shelf-life.
storageAdvice: Store below 25°C in the original amber glass bottle. Discard 3 months after opening.
defaultDirections: Dissolve 1/2 to 1 tablet under tongue at onset of angina. Call 000 if unresolved after 10 mins.

commonDoses.label: Acute angina attack
commonDoses.directions: Dissolve 1 tablet under tongue. Repeat once in 5 mins if pain persists. Call 000 if not relieved.

warningNote: STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED with PDE5 inhibitors (Viagra/Cialis) — risk of fatal collapse.

name: Nitrolingual Pumpspray (glyceryl trinitrate 400mcg/spray 200 doses)
indication: Acute relief and prophylaxis of angina pectoris.
mechanismOfAction: Generates nitric oxide, causing rapid vascular smooth muscle relaxation, systemic venodilation, and reduction in myocardial preload.
counselingAdvice: Prime the pump before first use. Spray 1 or 2 doses under the tongue while sitting down. Do not inhale spray. Call 000 if pain persists 10 minutes after second spray.
cautionsAndContraindications: Strictly contraindicated with PDE-5 inhibitors (sildenafil, tadalafil). Contraindicated in severe aortic stenosis, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, or severe hypotension.
adverseEffects: Pounding headache, flushing, orthostatic hypotension, syncope, tachycardia.
monitoringAdvice: Review angina frequency and correct inhaler technique.
defaultDirections: Spray 1 to 2 metered doses under the tongue while seated at onset of chest pain.

commonDoses.label: Acute angina relief
commonDoses.directions: Spray 1-2 sprays under tongue. Sit down. If no relief in 5 mins, repeat once. Call 000 if pain continues.

warningNote: Contraindicated with PDE5 inhibitors (Viagra/Cialis) within 24-48 hours.

name: Imdur (isosorbide mononitrate 60mg modified-release tablet)
indication: Prophylactic treatment of angina pectoris.
mechanismOfAction: Releases nitric oxide, relaxing venous smooth muscle, reducing left ventricular end-diastolic pressure and myocardial wall tension.
counselingAdvice: Take once daily in the morning with a glass of water. Swallow whole; do not chew or crush. Once-daily morning dosing provides a daily nitrate-free interval to prevent tolerance.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated with PDE5 inhibitors. Contraindicated in circulatory shock, constrictive pericarditis, or severe anaemia.
adverseEffects: Headache (common, usually abates with continued therapy), hypotension, dizziness, reflex tachycardia.
monitoringAdvice: Blood pressure, orthostatic vitals, and frequency of breakthrough angina.
defaultDirections: Take 1 tablet every morning with a glass of water. Swallow whole.

commonDoses.label: Standard morning dose (60mg)
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet every morning to maintain nitrate-free interval.

commonDoses.label: Initiation titration (30mg morning)
commonDoses.directions: Take half tablet (30mg) each morning for 2-4 days, then 60mg.

warningNote: Strictly avoid PDE5 inhibitors (Viagra/Cialis); must dose in morning to avoid nitrate tolerance.

name: Entresto (sacubitril 49mg + valsartan 51mg tablet)
indication: Treatment of symptomatic chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) in adult patients.
mechanismOfAction: Sacubitril inhibits neprilysin (increasing vasoactive peptides including natriuretic peptides); valsartan blocks angiotensin II AT1 receptors.
pbsRestrictionNote: Authority Required: Chronic heart failure NYHA Class II-IV with LVEF <= 40% despite optimal ACEI/ARB therapy.
counselingAdvice: Take twice daily with or without food. MUST allow at least 36 hours washout after stopping an ACE inhibitor before starting Entresto (prevents severe angioedema).
cautionsAndContraindications: Strictly contraindicated with concurrent ACE inhibitors (36-hour washout mandatory) or history of angioedema. Contraindicated in pregnancy.
adverseEffects: Hypotension, hyperkalaemia, renal impairment, dizziness, cough, angioedema.
monitoringAdvice: Check serum potassium, eGFR, and blood pressure at 1-2 weeks after initiation and after each dose escalation.
defaultDirections: Take 1 tablet twice daily. Titrate to 97/103mg twice daily as tolerated.

commonDoses.label: Starting dose (49/51mg BD)
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet twice daily; check renal function in 2 weeks.

commonDoses.label: Target maintenance (97/103mg BD)
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 high-strength tablet twice daily.

commonDoses.label: Low start if ACE naive / eGFR low (24/26mg BD)
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 low-strength tablet twice daily.

warningNote: MANDATORY 36-hour washout period when switching from an ACE inhibitor to prevent fatal angioedema.

name: Coversyl Plus (perindopril arginine 5mg + indapamide 1.25mg tablet)
drugClass: ACE Inhibitor and Thiazide-like Diuretic Combination
indication: Treatment of essential hypertension not adequately controlled by monotherapy.
mechanismOfAction: Perindopril inhibits angiotensin-converting enzyme reducing angiotensin II; indapamide promotes sodium and water excretion in the distal tubule and reduces vascular resistance.
counselingAdvice: Take once daily in the morning before food. Stay well-hydrated. Stand up slowly to avoid postural dizziness.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in pregnancy, bilateral renal artery stenosis, severe renal failure (eGFR < 30 mL/min), or history of ACEI-induced angioedema.
adverseEffects: Persistent dry cough, hypotension, dizziness, hypokalaemia, hyponatraemia, hyperuricaemia, renal impairment.
monitoringAdvice: Baseline and periodic monitoring of electrolytes, urea, creatinine, and eGFR.
storageAdvice: Store below 30°C in the original container.
defaultDirections: Take 1 tablet once daily in the morning before breakfast.

commonDoses.label: Standard daily morning dose
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet every morning before food.

warningNote: Contraindicated in pregnancy (Category D). Monitor potassium and renal function.

name: Twynsta (telmisartan 80mg + amlodipine 5mg tablet)
drugClass: Angiotensin II Receptor Blocker (ARB) and Dihydropyridine CCB
indication: Treatment of essential hypertension in patients not adequately controlled on single-agent monotherapy.
mechanismOfAction: Telmisartan selectively antagonises AT1 receptors; amlodipine inhibits transmembrane influx of calcium ions into vascular smooth muscle, causing peripheral vasodilation.
counselingAdvice: Take once daily with or without food. Protect tablets from moisture by keeping them in the blister pack until immediately before use.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in pregnancy (Category D), biliary obstructive disorders, severe hepatic impairment, or cardiogenic shock.
adverseEffects: Peripheral oedema, dizziness, flushing, fatigue, headache, hyperkalaemia, hypotension.
monitoringAdvice: Monitor blood pressure, potassium, and renal function.
storageAdvice: Store below 25°C in the original blister pack.
defaultDirections: Take 1 tablet once daily with water.

commonDoses.label: Standard combination
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet once daily in the morning.

commonDoses.label: High strength amlodipine (80/10mg)
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet daily if blood pressure requires higher amlodipine.

name: Exforge (amlodipine 5mg + valsartan 80mg tablet)
drugClass: Dihydropyridine Calcium Channel Blocker and ARB
indication: Treatment of essential hypertension in patients whose blood pressure is not adequately controlled on monotherapy.
mechanismOfAction: Dual arterial vasodilation via L-type calcium channel blockade and selective angiotensin II type 1 receptor antagonism.
counselingAdvice: Take once daily with or without food. Report ankle swelling or dizziness.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in pregnancy, severe hepatic impairment, biliary cirrhosis, and shock.
adverseEffects: Peripheral oedema, headache, nasopharyngitis, dizziness, fatigue, flushing.
monitoringAdvice: Blood pressure and renal electrolytes.
defaultDirections: Take 1 tablet once daily with water.

commonDoses.label: Standard 5/80mg daily
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet once daily.

commonDoses.label: Step up 5/160mg daily
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet once daily for resistant hypertension.

name: Isoptin SR (verapamil hydrochloride 180mg sustained-release tablet)
indication: Essential hypertension, prophylactic management of chronic stable angina, rate control in supraventricular tachyarrhythmias.
mechanismOfAction: Inhibits calcium ion influx across cardiac muscle and vascular smooth muscle; depresses SA and AV nodal conduction and reduces myocardial contractility.
counselingAdvice: Take with food in the morning. Swallow whole, do not crush or chew. Constipation is very common; maintain high fluid and dietary fibre intake.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in second- or third-degree AV block, sick sinus syndrome (without pacemaker), severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction, or combination with IV beta-blockers.
adverseEffects: Constipation (up to 30%), bradycardia, AV block, hypotension, dizziness, peripheral oedema, gingival hyperplasia.
monitoringAdvice: Baseline ECG (PR interval), heart rate, and blood pressure.
defaultDirections: Take 1 tablet once daily with breakfast. Swallow whole.

commonDoses.label: Standard hypertension / angina
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet once daily with breakfast.

commonDoses.label: Titrated dose (240mg)
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 240mg SR tablet once daily with breakfast.

warningNote: DO NOT combine with beta-blockers without specialist advice (severe bradycardia / AV block risk).

name: Tenormin / Noten (atenolol 50mg tablet)
indication: Hypertension, chronic stable angina pectoris, secondary prevention post-myocardial infarction, supraventricular arrhythmias.
mechanismOfAction: Selectively competes with catecholamines at cardiac beta-1 receptors, decreasing resting and exercise heart rate, myocardial contractility, and cardiac output.
counselingAdvice: Take once daily at the same time each day. Do not stop abruptly as rebound hypertension or angina may occur.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in severe bradycardia, second- or third-degree heart block, cardiogenic shock, and severe peripheral vascular disease.
adverseEffects: Cold extremities, bradycardia, fatigue, sleep disturbances, vivid dreams, bronchospasm (in susceptible asthmatics).
monitoringAdvice: Heart rate and blood pressure; renal clearance (primarily renally excreted).
defaultDirections: Take 1 tablet once daily with water.

commonDoses.label: Standard daily dose
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet once daily.

commonDoses.label: Low start / elderly
commonDoses.directions: Take half tablet (25mg) once daily.

warningNote: Do not cease abruptly; taper gradually to prevent rebound ischaemia.

name: Nebilet (nebivolol 5mg tablet)
drugClass: Third-generation Beta-1 Blocker with Vasodilating Properties
indication: Essential hypertension; stable mild to moderate chronic heart failure in addition to standard therapies in elderly patients.
mechanismOfAction: Highly selective beta-1 adrenergic antagonist with nitric oxide-mediated endothelial vasodilatory properties.
counselingAdvice: Take once daily with or without food at the same time each day.
cautionsAndContraindications: Severe bradycardia, AV block > first degree, acute decompensated heart failure, severe hepatic impairment.
adverseEffects: Headache, dizziness, paresthesias, dyspnea, constipation, nausea, bradycardia, oedema.
monitoringAdvice: Heart rate, blood pressure, and signs of heart failure.
defaultDirections: Take 1 tablet once daily at the same time each day.

commonDoses.label: Standard hypertension
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet once daily.

commonDoses.label: Heart failure initiation
commonDoses.directions: Start at 1.25mg daily and titrate at 1-2 week intervals.

name: Mounjaro (tirzepatide 5mg/0.5mL pre-filled pen)
drugClass: Dual GIP and GLP-1 Receptor Agonist
indication: Treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus as an adjunct to diet and exercise; chronic weight management in adults with obesity (BMI >= 30) or overweight (BMI >= 27) with comorbidities.
mechanismOfAction: First-in-class dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist that enhances insulin secretion, suppresses glucagon, delays gastric emptying, and centrally reduces appetite.
pbsRestrictionNote: Private prescription in Australia for weight loss / type 2 diabetes.
counselingAdvice: Inject subcutaneously once weekly into abdomen, thigh, or upper arm on the same day each week, any time of day, with or without food. Drink plenty of water and eat smaller, slower meals to prevent nausea.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in patients with personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) or Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN 2). Use caution in prior pancreatitis.
adverseEffects: Nausea, diarrhoea, vomiting, decreased appetite, constipation, dyspepsia, abdominal pain, fatigue, reflux.
monitoringAdvice: Monitor glycemic control, renal function (especially if vomiting/dehydration occurs), and signs of pancreatitis or gallbladder disease.
storageAdvice: Store in refrigerator (2°C to 8°C). Do not freeze. May be stored at room temperature below 30°C for up to 21 days.
defaultDirections: Inject 5mg subcutaneously once weekly into abdomen or thigh. Rotate injection sites.

commonDoses.label: Step-up maintenance (5mg weekly)
commonDoses.directions: Inject 5mg once weekly subcutaneously.

commonDoses.label: Initiation titration (2.5mg weekly x 4w)
commonDoses.directions: Inject 2.5mg once weekly for the first 4 weeks before increasing to 5mg.

commonDoses.label: High-dose escalation (10mg weekly)
commonDoses.directions: Inject 10mg once weekly if additional weight/glycemic response needed.

warningNote: Contraindicated with personal/family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN 2.

name: Wegovy (semaglutide 1mg/0.5mL pre-filled pen)
indication: Adjunct to a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity for chronic weight management in adults with BMI >= 30, or BMI >= 27 with weight-related comorbidities.
mechanismOfAction: Selectively activates GLP-1 receptors in the hypothalamus and hindbrain, increasing satiety, decreasing hunger, and slowing gastric emptying.
pbsRestrictionNote: Private prescription in Australia for chronic weight management.
counselingAdvice: Inject once weekly subcutaneously on the same day each week. Follow the 4-week dose titration schedule (0.25mg -> 0.5mg -> 1.0mg -> 1.7mg -> 2.4mg) to minimise GI side effects. Discontinue immediately if pregnancy is suspected.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in pregnancy and breastfeeding; personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC); history of pancreatitis.
adverseEffects: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, constipation, abdominal pain, headache, fatigue, cholelithiasis.
monitoringAdvice: Weight, blood pressure, renal function if dehydration occurs, signs of acute pancreatitis.
storageAdvice: Store at 2°C to 8°C (Refrigerate). Do not freeze. May be kept below 30°C for up to 28 days.
defaultDirections: Inject 1mg subcutaneously once weekly into abdomen, thigh, or upper arm.

commonDoses.label: Intermediate titration (1mg weekly)
commonDoses.directions: Inject 1mg once weekly subcutaneously for 4 weeks.

commonDoses.label: Target maintenance (2.4mg weekly)
commonDoses.directions: Inject 2.4mg once weekly subcutaneously as ongoing maintenance.

commonDoses.label: Starting titration (0.25mg weekly)
commonDoses.directions: Inject 0.25mg once weekly for weeks 1 to 4.

warningNote: Must titrate in 4-week steps to avoid severe nausea/vomiting; Category D in pregnancy.

name: Saxenda (liraglutide 6mg/mL pre-filled pen 3mL)
indication: Adjunct to lifestyle modification for weight management in adult patients with BMI >= 30, or BMI >= 27 with comorbidity.
mechanismOfAction: Human GLP-1 receptor agonist that regulates appetite by increasing feelings of fullness and satiety while dampening hunger cues.
counselingAdvice: Inject subcutaneously once daily at any time of day, independent of meals. Increase dose by 0.6mg weekly to target maintenance dose of 3.0mg daily.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in pregnancy; history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or pancreatitis.
adverseEffects: Nausea, diarrhoea, constipation, vomiting, injection site reactions, hypoglycemia (if combined with sulfonylureas).
monitoringAdvice: Assess weight at 12 weeks on 3.0mg/day; discontinue if >= 5% weight loss not achieved.
storageAdvice: Store in refrigerator (2°C to 8°C). After first use, store below 30°C for up to 30 days.
defaultDirections: Inject subcutaneously once daily. Titrate weekly from 0.6mg to 3.0mg daily.

commonDoses.label: Maintenance dose (3.0mg daily)
commonDoses.directions: Inject 3.0mg subcutaneously once daily.

commonDoses.label: Initial titration (0.6mg daily)
commonDoses.directions: Inject 0.6mg daily for week 1, increasing weekly by 0.6mg.

name: Duromine (phentermine 30mg modified-release capsule)
indication: Short-term (up to 12 weeks) adjunctive management of moderate to severe obesity (BMI >= 30 or BMI >= 27 with risk factors).
mechanismOfAction: Sympathomimetic stimulant that enhances noradrenaline release in the hypothalamus, depressing hunger and increasing metabolic rate.
counselingAdvice: Take first thing in the morning with breakfast to avoid nocturnal insomnia. Swallow whole. Avoid caffeine. Limit treatment to maximum 12 weeks.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in uncontrolled hypertension, cardiovascular disease, hyperthyroidism, glaucoma, history of psychiatric illness or substance abuse, concurrent MAOIs.
adverseEffects: Insomnia, dry mouth, tachycardia, elevated blood pressure, nervousness, tremor, palpitations, restlessness.
monitoringAdvice: Monitor blood pressure and pulse rate at baseline and every 2 to 4 weeks. Assess psychological state.
defaultDirections: Take 1 capsule every morning at breakfast. Swallow whole. Do not take in the afternoon.

commonDoses.label: Standard morning dose (30mg)
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 capsule every morning at breakfast for up to 12 weeks.

commonDoses.label: Low dose / sensitive patients (15mg)
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 15mg capsule every morning with food.

commonDoses.label: High dose (40mg)
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 40mg capsule once daily in morning.

warningNote: SafeScript monitored in several states; contraindicated with uncontrolled hypertension or cardiovascular disease.

name: Cialis (tadalafil 20mg tablet)
indication: Treatment of erectile dysfunction in adult men; pulmonary arterial hypertension.
mechanismOfAction: Inhibits PDE5, preventing the degradation of cGMP in the corpus cavernosum, promoting smooth muscle relaxation and inflow of blood during sexual stimulation. Long duration of action (up to 36 hours).
pbsRestrictionNote: Private prescription for erectile dysfunction.
counselingAdvice: Take at least 30 to 60 minutes before anticipated sexual activity. Effective for up to 36 hours ('the weekend pill'). Requires sexual stimulation to work. Do not exceed 1 tablet per day.
cautionsAndContraindications: STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED with any form of organic nitrates (glyceryl trinitrate, isosorbide) or guanylate cyclase stimulators (riociguat) — severe fatal hypotension.
adverseEffects: Headache, dyspepsia, back pain, myalgia, nasal congestion, flushing, transient visual disturbance.
monitoringAdvice: Cardiovascular status and tolerance for sexual exertion.
defaultFrequency: As needed prior to sexual activity
defaultDirections: Take 1 tablet at least 30 to 60 minutes prior to anticipated sexual activity. Max 1 tablet in 24 hours.

commonDoses.label: On-demand (20mg PRN)
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet 30-60 mins before sexual activity. Max 1 daily.

commonDoses.label: Daily low-dose (5mg once daily)
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 5mg tablet once daily at approx same time each day.

warningNote: STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED with nitrates (anginine, nitrolingual, imdur) — fatal collapse.

name: Testogel (testosterone 50mg/5g transdermal gel sachets)
indication: Testosterone replacement therapy for male hypogonadism confirmed by clinical features and low serum testosterone.
mechanismOfAction: Exogenous testosterone binds to androgen receptors, promoting male secondary sexual characteristics, libido, bone density, and muscle mass.
pbsRestrictionNote: Authority Required: Pathological hypogonadism proven by baseline low serum testosterone levels.
counselingAdvice: Apply once daily in the morning to clean, dry, intact skin of the shoulders, arms, or abdomen. Wash hands immediately with soap and water. Cover application area with clothing to avoid secondary transfer to women or children.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in suspected or confirmed carcinoma of the prostate or male breast cancer. Contraindicated in pregnancy and women.
adverseEffects: Skin irritation, erythrocytosis (elevated haematocrit), acne, alopecia, gynaecomastia, mood swings, fluid retention.
monitoringAdvice: Serum testosterone, haematocrit/haemoglobin, PSA, and digital rectal examination at baseline, 3, 6, and 12 months.
defaultDirections: Apply the contents of 1 sachet (50mg) to clean, dry shoulders/arms once daily in the morning.

commonDoses.label: Standard daily gel sachet
commonDoses.directions: Apply 1 sachet daily in the morning to shoulders or abdomen.

warningNote: Prevent contact transfer to women and children; monitor haematocrit and PSA.

name: Diane-35 ED / Estelle-35 ED (cyproterone 2mg + ethinylestradiol 35mcg tablet)
indication: Treatment of severe acne refractory to prolonged oral antibiotic therapy and/or moderately severe hirsutism in women of reproductive age.
mechanismOfAction: Cyproterone blocks androgen receptors and inhibits 5-alpha-reductase; ethinylestradiol increases sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG) to reduce free circulating androgens.
pbsRestrictionNote: Restricted Benefit: Severe acne or hirsutism unresponsive to other treatments.
counselingAdvice: Take 1 tablet daily at the same time each day for 28 consecutive days without interruption. Provides effective contraception; do not use another hormonal contraceptive simultaneously. Higher VTE risk than other low-dose COCs.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in smokers aged >= 35, history of venous thromboembolism, arterial thrombosis, migraine with aura, breast cancer, severe hepatic disease.
adverseEffects: Venous thromboembolism (VTE), breast tenderness, breakthrough bleeding, nausea, headache, melasma, mood alteration.
monitoringAdvice: Blood pressure and screening for thromboembolic symptoms (leg swelling, sudden chest pain or shortness of breath).
defaultDirections: Take 1 tablet daily at the same time each day following the blister pack sequence.

commonDoses.label: Standard 28-day cycle
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet daily following blister arrows.

warningNote: Higher risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE) than second-generation pills. Strictly contraindicated with migraine with aura.

name: Yaz (drospirenone 3mg + ethinylestradiol 20mcg tablet 28s)
indication: Oral contraception, treatment of moderate acne vulgaris in women seeking contraception, treatment of premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD).
mechanismOfAction: Suppresses gonadotropins to inhibit ovulation; drospirenone is a spironolactone analogue with anti-mineralocorticoid and anti-androgenic activity.
counselingAdvice: Take 1 tablet daily at approximately the same time for 28 days (24 active pink tablets followed by 4 white inactive tablets). May reduce water retention and bloating.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in women aged >= 35 who smoke, migraine with aura, active/history of VTE, renal impairment (hyperkalaemia risk).
adverseEffects: Headache, nausea, breast tenderness, irregular bleeding, mood changes, thromboembolism, hyperkalaemia.
monitoringAdvice: Baseline blood pressure and periodic review.
defaultDirections: Take 1 tablet daily at the same time without missing doses.

commonDoses.label: Continuous 28-day pack
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet daily following blister foil arrows.

warningNote: Drospirenone possesses mild potassium-sparing properties; avoid in renal insufficiency.

name: Mirena (levonorgestrel 52mg intrauterine delivery system)
indication: Long-acting reversible contraception; treatment of idiopathic menorrhagia (heavy menstrual bleeding); endometrial protection during estrogen replacement therapy.
mechanismOfAction: Locally releases levonorgestrel into uterine cavity, causing profound endometrial atrophy, thickening of cervical mucus, and suppression of sperm motility.
counselingAdvice: Effective for up to 8 years for contraception (5 years for menorrhagia/HRT). Irregular spotting is common during the first 3 to 6 months before menses become very light or absent (amenorrhoea). Check strings monthly.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in active pelvic inflammatory disease, pregnancy, unexplained uterine bleeding, cervical/uterine malignancy, distorted uterine cavity.
adverseEffects: Intermenstrual spotting/bleeding, amenorrhoea, pelvic discomfort, ovarian cysts, expulsion, uterine perforation (< 1 in 1000 insertions).
monitoringAdvice: Post-insertion check at 6 weeks to confirm thread position and exclude expulsion.
defaultFrequency: Inserted by certified medical practitioner (effective up to 8 years)
defaultDirections: One device inserted intrauterinely by trained medical practitioner.

commonDoses.label: Intrauterine insertion (single device)
commonDoses.directions: For insertion by credentialed clinician under aseptic technique.

warningNote: Exclude pregnancy and active pelvic infection before insertion.

name: Vagifem (estradiol 10mcg vaginal tablet with applicator 24s)
indication: Treatment of atrophic vaginitis due to estrogen deficiency in postmenopausal women.
mechanismOfAction: Locally replaces declining estradiol in vaginal tissues, restoring normal vaginal epithelium, glycogen production, acidic pH, and natural lubrication with minimal systemic absorption.
pbsRestrictionNote: Restricted Benefit: Atrophic vaginitis in postmenopausal women.
counselingAdvice: Insert 1 tablet vaginally using the supplied single-use applicator once daily for 2 weeks, then reduce to maintenance of 1 tablet twice weekly. Does not require systemic progestogen for endometrial protection at this dose.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in unexplained abnormal vaginal bleeding, active or suspected breast or estrogen-dependent cancer, active deep vein thrombosis.
adverseEffects: Mild vaginal discharge, pruritus, transient vaginal discomfort or bleeding.
monitoringAdvice: Annual gynaecological assessment; investigate any unexpected vaginal bleeding immediately.
defaultDirections: Insert 1 tablet vaginally daily for 2 weeks, then maintenance of 1 tablet twice weekly (e.g. Mon & Thu).

commonDoses.label: Maintenance twice weekly
commonDoses.directions: Insert 1 vaginal tablet twice weekly (e.g. Monday and Thursday).

commonDoses.label: Initial loading (14 days daily)
commonDoses.directions: Insert 1 vaginal tablet nightly for the first 14 consecutive days.

name: Ativan (lorazepam 1mg tablet)
indication: Short-term relief of severe anxiety; premedication before surgery; status epilepticus (parenteral).
mechanismOfAction: Enhances gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) inhibitory neurotransmission by binding to GABA-A receptor benzodiazepine sites.
counselingAdvice: For short-term use only (maximum 2 to 4 weeks). May cause drowsiness; do not drive or operate machinery. Avoid alcohol completely. Dependence and withdrawal occur with prolonged use.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in severe respiratory depression, myasthenia gravis, sleep apnoea. High risk of dependence and tolerance.
adverseEffects: Sedation, dizziness, ataxia, cognitive impairment, anterograde amnesia, respiratory depression, rebound anxiety on withdrawal.
monitoringAdvice: Review regularly; limit prescription quantities and monitor via state real-time prescription monitoring (SafeScript).
storageAdvice: Store below 25°C in a dry place.
defaultFrequency: Twice to three times daily as needed
defaultDirections: Take 0.5 to 1 tablet as needed for severe acute anxiety. Maximum 3mg daily. Short-term use only.

commonDoses.label: Acute anxiety (1mg PRN)
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet as needed for severe anxiety. Max 2 tablets in 24 hours.

commonDoses.label: Low dose / elderly (0.5mg)
commonDoses.directions: Take half tablet (0.5mg) as needed.

warningNote: SafeScript monitored. High risk of tolerance, physical dependence, and cognitive slowing.

name: Rivotril / Paxam (clonazepam 0.5mg tablet)
indication: Epilepsy in adults and children (absence, myoclonic, tonic-clonic); panic disorder; severe restless legs syndrome.
mechanismOfAction: Potentiates GABA-ergic neurotransmission by binding to the GABA-A receptor complex, suppressing epileptogenic foci and hyperarousal.
counselingAdvice: Take at night or split into divided doses. Causes drowsiness; avoid alcohol. Do not stop abruptly as seizures or severe withdrawal can occur.
cautionsAndContraindications: Severe respiratory insufficiency, myasthenia gravis, acute narrow-angle glaucoma.
adverseEffects: Somnolence, fatigue, muscular hypotonia, ataxia, impaired coordination, paradoxical excitement.
monitoringAdvice: SafeScript real-time prescription monitoring; taper slowly when stopping.
defaultDirections: Take 1 tablet (0.5mg) at bedtime or twice daily as prescribed.

commonDoses.label: Nocturnal panic / seizure
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet (0.5mg) at bedtime.

commonDoses.label: Divided dose (0.5mg BD)
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet in the morning and 1 tablet at night.

warningNote: SafeScript monitored. Do not cease abruptly due to risk of withdrawal seizures.

name: Kalma / Alprax (alprazolam 0.5mg tablet)
indication: Short-term treatment of extreme, disabling anxiety and panic disorder refractory to other treatments.
mechanismOfAction: Binds to benzodiazepine receptors facilitating GABA action. Schedule 8 controlled medicine in Australia due to high abuse and dependence potential.
pbsRestrictionNote: Authority Required: Schedule 8 medicine. Severe panic disorder unresponsive to other pharmacotherapy.
counselingAdvice: Strictly for short-term use. High potential for dependence and severe rebound anxiety. Do not drive or operate machinery. Do not mix with alcohol or opioids.
cautionsAndContraindications: Schedule 8 controlled substance in Australia. Contraindicated with concurrent opioids, sleep apnoea, or substance abuse history.
adverseEffects: Profound sedation, memory impairment, dependence, tolerance, ataxia, rebound anxiety.
monitoringAdvice: State health authority S8 permit / SafeScript mandatory before prescribing.
defaultDirections: Take 0.5 tablet to 1 tablet as strictly directed. Short-term only.

commonDoses.label: Panic attack relief (0.5mg)
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet as strictly authorized.

warningNote: SCHEDULE 8 CONTROLLED DRUG in Australia. State S8 permit and SafeScript review mandatory.

name: Imovane (zopiclone 7.5mg tablet)
indication: Short-term treatment of severe insomnia (difficulty falling asleep, nocturnal awakenings) in adults.
mechanismOfAction: Binds selectively to alpha-1 subunit of GABA-A receptor complex, modulating GABA transmission to promote sleep architecture.
counselingAdvice: Take immediately before going to bed. Ensure 7-8 hours of uninterrupted sleep. Do not take with alcohol. May cause a bitter or metallic taste in the mouth next morning. Limit use to 2-4 weeks.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in severe sleep apnoea, severe hepatic impairment, myasthenia gravis. Avoid complex sleep behaviours (sleep-walking, sleep-driving).
adverseEffects: Bitter/metallic taste (dysgeusia), morning somnolence, dry mouth, headache, dizziness, anterograde amnesia, parasomnias.
monitoringAdvice: SafeScript monitored in Australia. Re-evaluate cause of insomnia if persistent beyond 2 weeks.
defaultDirections: Take 1 tablet with water immediately before retiring to bed. Maximum 2 to 4 weeks.

commonDoses.label: Standard bedtime dose (7.5mg)
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet immediately before bed. Ensure 8h in bed.

commonDoses.label: Elderly dose (3.75mg - half tablet)
commonDoses.directions: Take half tablet (3.75mg) immediately before retiring to bed.

warningNote: SafeScript monitored; report any complex sleep behaviours (e.g. sleep-driving).

name: Cymbalta (duloxetine 60mg delayed-release capsule)
indication: Major depressive disorder, generalised anxiety disorder, diabetic peripheral neuropathic pain, fibromyalgia.
mechanismOfAction: Potent dual reuptake inhibitor of both serotonin (5-HT) and noradrenaline (NA), enhancing descending inhibitory pain pathways and mood regulation.
counselingAdvice: Swallow whole with or without food. Do not chew or crush. Antidepressant onset takes 2 to 4 weeks. Do not cease abruptly due to severe electric-shock-like discontinuation symptoms.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated with MAO inhibitors or uncontrolled narrow-angle glaucoma. Caution in severe hepatic impairment or heavy alcohol use.
adverseEffects: Nausea (common in first 2 weeks), dry mouth, somnolence or insomnia, sweating, constipation, elevated blood pressure, sexual dysfunction.
monitoringAdvice: Monitor blood pressure and pulse rate; monitor mood and suicidality during initial weeks; taper slowly over weeks when stopping.
defaultDirections: Take 1 capsule once daily in the morning with food. Swallow whole.

commonDoses.label: Standard daily maintenance (60mg)
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 capsule every morning with breakfast.

commonDoses.label: Starter dose (30mg daily x 1-2 weeks)
commonDoses.directions: Take 30mg daily for 1 to 2 weeks to reduce nausea, then 60mg.

warningNote: Taper slowly upon discontinuation to prevent severe SNRI withdrawal syndrome.

name: Zyprexa (olanzapine 5mg tablet)
indication: Schizophrenia, manic episodes of bipolar disorder, maintenance treatment in bipolar I disorder.
mechanismOfAction: Antagonises multiple neuroreceptors: serotonin 5-HT2A/2C, dopamine D1-D4, histamine H1, and alpha-1 adrenergic receptors.
counselingAdvice: Take once daily in the evening at bedtime due to marked sedation. Weight gain and increased appetite are common; maintain healthy diet and regular physical activity.
cautionsAndContraindications: Caution in diabetes mellitus, dyslipidaemia, cardiovascular disease, or elderly with dementia-related psychosis.
adverseEffects: Weight gain, somnolence, hypertriglyceridaemia, hypercholesterolaemia, insulin resistance, anticholinergic effects, orthostatic hypotension.
monitoringAdvice: Baseline and 3-monthly weight, waist circumference, fasting blood glucose / HbA1c, and fasting lipid profile.
storageAdvice: Store below 25°C. Protect from light and moisture.
defaultDirections: Take 1 tablet once daily at bedtime with water.

commonDoses.label: Initial / Low-dose (5mg nocte)
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet (5mg) at bedtime.

commonDoses.label: Therapeutic maintenance (10mg nocte)
commonDoses.directions: Take 10mg once daily at bedtime.

warningNote: Significant risk of rapid metabolic weight gain, dyslipidaemia, and new-onset diabetes.

name: Rexulti (brexpiprazole 2mg tablet)
indication: Treatment of schizophrenia in adults; adjunctive therapy to antidepressants for major depressive disorder.
mechanismOfAction: Partial agonist at serotonin 5-HT1A and dopamine D2 receptors; antagonist at serotonin 5-HT2A and noradrenaline alpha-1B/2C receptors.
pbsRestrictionNote: Authority Required: Schizophrenia in adults.
counselingAdvice: Take once daily with or without food. Report restlessness or inability to sit still (akathisia).
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis.
adverseEffects: Weight gain, akathisia, somnolence, dyspepsia, tremor, nasopharyngitis.
monitoringAdvice: Metabolic parameters (weight, fasting glucose, lipids) and motor symptoms for akathisia.
defaultDirections: Take 1 tablet once daily with water.

commonDoses.label: Target maintenance (2mg daily)
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet once daily.

commonDoses.label: Initiation titration (1mg daily)
commonDoses.directions: Take 1mg once daily for days 1 to 4, then titrate to 2mg.

name: Ritalin (methylphenidate hydrochloride 10mg tablet)
indication: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) in adults and children; narcolepsy.
mechanismOfAction: Blocks reuptake of dopamine and noradrenaline into presynaptic neurons by inhibiting DAT and NET transporters.
pbsRestrictionNote: Authority Required: ADHD diagnosed by psychiatrist or paediatrician in accordance with state stimulant prescribing regulations.
counselingAdvice: Take in the morning and early afternoon (e.g. 8am and 12pm). Avoid late afternoon or evening dosing to prevent insomnia. Take with meals to reduce appetite suppression.
cautionsAndContraindications: Schedule 8 medicine. Contraindicated in severe anxiety, glaucoma, thyrotoxicosis, structural cardiac abnormalities, cardiomyopathy, or concurrent MAOIs.
adverseEffects: Appetite suppression, weight loss, insomnia, tachycardia, hypertension, palpitations, dry mouth, headache, irritability.
monitoringAdvice: Blood pressure, heart rate, weight, height (in children), and SafeScript / state S8 permit compliance.
storageAdvice: Store below 25°C in a locked cabinet.
defaultDirections: Take 1 tablet in the morning and 1 tablet at lunchtime with meals.

commonDoses.label: Standard BD dosing (10mg morning + noon)
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet at 8am and 1 tablet at 12pm with food.

commonDoses.label: Starter dose (5mg morning)
commonDoses.directions: Take half tablet (5mg) with breakfast.

warningNote: SCHEDULE 8 STIMULANT. Requires valid state specialist endorsement / stimulant permit.

name: Topamax (topiramate 50mg tablet)
indication: Prophylaxis of migraine in adults; monotherapy or adjunctive therapy for generalised tonic-clonic or partial onset seizures.
mechanismOfAction: Blocks voltage-dependent sodium channels, potentiates GABA inhibitory activity, and antagonises AMPA/kainate glutamate receptors.
counselingAdvice: Drink plenty of water to reduce the risk of kidney stones. Titrate slowly upwards to minimise cognitive slowing ('Dopamax' word-finding difficulty). May reduce oral contraceptive efficacy.
cautionsAndContraindications: Strictly contraindicated in pregnancy (Category D: high risk of cleft lip/palate, neurodevelopmental disorders). Avoid carbonic anhydrase inhibitors.
adverseEffects: Paresthesias (tingling in fingers/toes), cognitive slowing, word-finding difficulty, anorexia, weight loss, nephrolithiasis, metabolic acidosis, acute myopia/glaucoma.
monitoringAdvice: Monitor serum bicarbonate (metabolic acidosis), renal function, and weight.
storageAdvice: Store below 25°C in a dry place.
defaultDirections: Take 1 tablet twice daily with water.

commonDoses.label: Migraine prophylaxis target (50mg BD)
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet (50mg) morning and evening with water.

commonDoses.label: Initiation titration (25mg nocte)
commonDoses.directions: Take 25mg at bedtime for week 1, then titrate weekly by 25mg.

warningNote: High risk of congenital cleft palate (Category D). Paresthesias and word-finding issues common.

name: Panadeine Forte (paracetamol 500mg + codeine phosphate 30mg tablet)
indication: Short-term relief of acute moderate to severe pain not responding to simpler analgesics.
mechanismOfAction: Paracetamol acts on central prostaglandin synthesis; codeine is metabolized by CYP2D6 into morphine, binding to mu-opioid receptors.
pbsRestrictionNote: Restricted Benefit: Severe acute pain unresponsive to non-opioids. Maximum 20 tablets without repeats.
counselingAdvice: Take with food or water. Do not exceed 8 tablets in 24 hours. Do not take any other paracetamol-containing products. Causes constipation; use a stool softener if needed.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in ultra-rapid CYP2D6 metabolisers, children under 12, breastfeeding mothers (risk of infant morphine toxicity), respiratory depression.
adverseEffects: Constipation, nausea, somnolence, dizziness, vomiting, dependence, respiratory depression in overdose.
monitoringAdvice: SafeScript monitored across Australia; assess risk of opioid dependence.
defaultFrequency: Every 4 to 6 hours as needed for pain
defaultDirections: Take 1 to 2 tablets every 4 to 6 hours as needed for severe pain. Max 8 tablets in 24 hours.

commonDoses.label: Acute severe pain (1-2 tabs Q4-6H)
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 or 2 tablets every 4-6 hours PRN (max 8 tablets daily).

warningNote: SafeScript monitored. Do not combine with other paracetamol products; ultra-rapid metabolisers risk toxicity.

name: Durogesic (fentanyl 25mcg/hour transdermal patch)
indication: Management of chronic severe intractable pain of cancer or non-cancer origin in opioid-tolerant patients requiring continuous opioid administration.
mechanismOfAction: Pure mu-opioid receptor agonist with high lipid solubility, delivered transdermally for systemic analgesia over 72 hours.
pbsRestrictionNote: Authority Required: Chronic severe disabling pain in patients who are already opioid tolerant.
counselingAdvice: Apply 1 patch every 72 hours (3 days) to clean, dry, hairless skin on upper torso. Avoid exposing patch to direct heat (heating pads, saunas, hot baths - increases release rate and risk of fatal overdose). Fold used patch adhesive-side in before safe disposal.
cautionsAndContraindications: STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED in opioid-naive patients (causes fatal respiratory depression). Contraindicated in acute or post-operative pain.
adverseEffects: Fatal respiratory depression, somnolence, constipation, nausea, vomiting, erythema under patch, physical dependence.
monitoringAdvice: Strict SafeScript and state S8 permit compliance. Monitor respiratory rate, sedation, and opioid withdrawal signs during patch changes.
storageAdvice: Store below 25°C in original pouch. Keep locked in secure medicine cabinet.
defaultDirections: Apply 1 patch every 72 hours to intact skin on upper trunk or arm. Rotate application sites.

commonDoses.label: Standard 72-hour patch rotation
commonDoses.directions: Apply 1 patch every 3 days. Remove previous patch before applying new one.

warningNote: SCHEDULE 8 OPIOID. STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED IN OPIOID-NAIVE PATIENTS — FATAL OVERDOSE RISK.

name: MS Contin (morphine sulfate 30mg controlled-release tablet)
indication: Prolonged relief of chronic severe pain unresponsive to non-opioid analgesics, particularly cancer pain.
mechanismOfAction: Principal alkaloid of opium; full mu-opioid receptor agonist in the CNS and gastrointestinal tract.
pbsRestrictionNote: Authority Required: Chronic severe disabling pain.
counselingAdvice: Take every 12 hours with water. Swallow whole; DO NOT BREAK, CRUSH, OR CHEW (destroys controlled-release mechanism causing dose-dumping and fatal overdose). Prescribe concurrent aperients.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in acute respiratory depression, paralytic ileus, severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, or concurrent MAOIs.
adverseEffects: Severe constipation, sedation, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, pruritus, respiratory depression, physical dependence.
monitoringAdvice: SafeScript mandatory; monitor bowel function continuously.
defaultDirections: Take 1 tablet every 12 hours with water. Swallow whole without chewing.

commonDoses.label: Standard 12-hourly chronic pain
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet every 12 hours (e.g. 8am and 8pm). Swallow whole.

warningNote: SCHEDULE 8. Swallow whole; DO NOT CRUSH — risk of fatal dose dumping.

name: Sinemet (levodopa 100mg + carbidopa 25mg tablet)
drugClass: Dopamine Precursor and Dopa Decarboxylase Inhibitor
indication: Treatment of Parkinson's disease and parkinsonian syndrome.
mechanismOfAction: Levodopa crosses the blood-brain barrier and is decarboxylated into dopamine in the brain; carbidopa inhibits peripheral decarboxylation, reducing nausea and increasing brain bioavailability.
counselingAdvice: Take 30 minutes before meals or 1 hour after meals for optimal absorption. Avoid taking with high-protein meals as amino acids compete for absorption. Take at strictly scheduled times.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated with non-selective MAO inhibitors, suspicious undiagnosed skin lesions or melanoma history, narrow-angle glaucoma.
adverseEffects: Nausea, orthostatic hypotension, dyskinesias, vivid dreams, hallucinations, impulse control disorders (gambling, hypersexuality).
monitoringAdvice: Assess motor fluctuations (on-off phenomena), involuntary movements, and orthostatic vitals.
defaultDirections: Take 1 tablet three times daily 30 minutes prior to meals at regular intervals.

commonDoses.label: Maintenance (1 tab TDS)
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet at 7am, 12pm, 5pm 30 mins before food.

commonDoses.label: Titration start (half tab TDS)
commonDoses.directions: Take half tablet 3 times daily for 3 days, then 1 tablet TDS.

name: Motilium (domperidone 10mg tablet)
drugClass: Peripheral Dopamine D2 Receptor Antagonist / Prokinetic
indication: Short-term relief of nausea and vomiting; diabetic gastroparesis.
mechanismOfAction: Blocks peripheral dopamine D2 receptors in the gastrointestinal tract and chemoreceptor trigger zone outside the blood-brain barrier, accelerating gastric emptying.
counselingAdvice: Take 15 to 30 minutes before meals. Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest possible duration (maximum 7 consecutive days).
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in conditions where cardiac conduction is impaired, prolonged QT intervals, or co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (QT prolongation / fatal ventricular arrhythmias).
adverseEffects: Dry mouth, headache, QT prolongation, galactorrhoea, amenorrhoea, gynaecomastia (hyperprolactinaemia).
monitoringAdvice: Baseline ECG if cardiac risk factors present; avoid in patients > 60 years taking > 30mg daily.
defaultDirections: Take 1 tablet up to 3 times daily 15-30 mins before food. Max 30mg daily for up to 7 days.

commonDoses.label: Nausea before meals (10mg TDS)
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet 15-30 minutes before each main meal.

warningNote: Risk of QT prolongation and ventricular arrhythmias — limit course to 7 days.

name: Janumet (sitagliptin 50mg + metformin hydrochloride 1000mg tablet)
indication: Treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control.
mechanismOfAction: Sitagliptin prolongs active incretin levels (GLP-1/GIP) stimulating insulin release; metformin reduces hepatic gluconeogenesis and improves peripheral insulin sensitivity.
pbsRestrictionNote: Restricted Benefit: Type 2 diabetes with HbA1c > 7% despite diet and metformin monotherapy.
counselingAdvice: Take twice daily with meals to reduce gastrointestinal upset. Withhold before iodinated radiocontrast procedures or surgery.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30 mL/min), acute metabolic acidosis, severe hepatic impairment.
adverseEffects: Diarrhoea, nausea, dyspepsia, nasopharyngitis, headache, pancreatitis (rare), lactic acidosis (rare).
monitoringAdvice: eGFR, renal function, and HbA1c every 3 to 6 months.
defaultDirections: Take 1 tablet twice daily with morning and evening meals.

commonDoses.label: Standard BD maintenance
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet with breakfast and 1 tablet with dinner.

warningNote: Withhold prior to iodinated CT contrast scans; contraindication eGFR < 30 mL/min.

name: Humalog (insulin lispro 100 U/mL 3mL pre-filled KwikPen)
indication: Treatment of diabetes mellitus requiring insulin for glucose homeostasis.
mechanismOfAction: Rapid-acting human insulin analogue with inverted amino acid sequence (LysB28, ProB29), speeding absorption and peak onset within 15 minutes of injection.
counselingAdvice: Inject subcutaneously immediately (0-15 minutes) before or right after a meal. Always carry fast-acting carbohydrates (jelly beans, glucose tablets) to treat hypoglycemia.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated during episodes of hypoglycemia.
adverseEffects: Hypoglycemia, injection site lipodystrophy, weight gain, peripheral oedema.
monitoringAdvice: Self-monitoring of blood glucose levels before and after meals; HbA1c every 3 months.
storageAdvice: Store unopened pens at 2°C to 8°C (Refrigerate). Pen in use can be kept at room temperature below 30°C for up to 28 days.
defaultFrequency: Three times daily immediately before meals
defaultDirections: Inject subcutaneously 0-15 minutes before meals according to carbohydrate ratio and blood glucose readings.

commonDoses.label: Pre-meal bolus dosing
commonDoses.directions: Inject prescribed units immediately before breakfast, lunch, dinner.

warningNote: Rapid onset within 15 minutes — ensure meal is ready before injecting.

name: Florinef (fludrocortisone acetate 100mcg tablet)
indication: Partial replacement therapy for primary and secondary adrenocortical insufficiency (Addison's disease); salt-losing adrenogenital syndrome; postural orthostatic hypotension refractory to non-pharmacologic measures.
mechanismOfAction: Acts on distal tubules to cause potassium and hydrogen excretion and sodium/water reabsorption, restoring plasma volume and arterial pressure.
counselingAdvice: Take once daily in the morning with food. Store in the refrigerator between 2°C and 8°C. Report swelling in ankles or rapid weight gain.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in systemic fungal infections or uncontrolled hypertension.
adverseEffects: Hypertension, oedema, hypokalaemia, headache, heart failure exacerbation.
monitoringAdvice: Regular blood pressure, serum electrolytes (potassium and sodium), and body weight.
storageAdvice: Store at 2°C to 8°C (Refrigerate). Protect from light.
defaultDirections: Take 1 tablet (100mcg) every morning with breakfast. Keep in refrigerator.

commonDoses.label: Standard Addison's mineralocorticoid
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet every morning with breakfast.

commonDoses.label: Low dose (50mcg daily)
commonDoses.directions: Take half tablet every morning.

warningNote: Store in refrigerator (2°C-8°C); monitor potassium and blood pressure.

name: Neo-Mercazole (carbimazole 5mg tablet)
indication: Treatment of hyperthyroidism (Graves' disease, toxic multinodular goitre); preparation for thyroidectomy or radioactive iodine therapy.
mechanismOfAction: Rapidly converted to methimazole, which inhibits thyroid peroxidase enzyme, preventing iodination of tyrosine residues in thyroglobulin.
counselingAdvice: Take with or without food at regular times each day. CRITICAL WARNING: Stop taking immediately and see a doctor for an urgent full blood count if you develop sore throat, fever, mouth ulcers, or any signs of infection (agranulocytosis risk).
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in severe preexisting haematological abnormalities or liver impairment.
adverseEffects: Agranulocytosis (< 0.5%, life-threatening), pruritus, rash, arthralgia, nausea, headache, mild transaminitis.
monitoringAdvice: Urgent FBC if fever/sore throat occurs. Regular thyroid function tests (FT3, FT4, TSH) every 4-6 weeks during titration.
storageAdvice: Store below 25°C in a dry place.
defaultDirections: Take 3 to 4 tablets daily as directed. Report sore throat or fever immediately.

commonDoses.label: Initiation dose (20mg daily)
commonDoses.directions: Take 4 tablets once daily in morning.

commonDoses.label: Maintenance dose (5-10mg daily)
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 to 2 tablets once daily based on FT4 levels.

warningNote: PATIENT ALERT: Discontinue immediately and check urgent FBC if sore throat or fever occurs (agranulocytosis).

name: Plaquenil (hydroxychloroquine sulfate 200mg tablet)
indication: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), rheumatoid arthritis, discoid lupus, juvenile idiopathic arthritis.
mechanismOfAction: Accumulates in lysosomes, increasing pH and inhibiting antigen presentation and toll-like receptor signaling; suppresses immune activation.
counselingAdvice: Take with food or milk to avoid stomach upset. Onset of clinical benefit may take 6 to 12 weeks. Regular eye examinations are mandatory to check for retinal toxicity.
cautionsAndContraindications: Preexisting maculopathy or retinopathy. Dose must not exceed 5mg/kg/day actual body weight to minimise retinal toxicity.
adverseEffects: Retinopathy (bull's-eye maculopathy), gastrointestinal discomfort, headache, skin rash, pigmentation, QT prolongation.
monitoringAdvice: Baseline ophthalmological screening (visual fields, OCT) within 1 year, and annual screening after 5 years (or sooner if high risk).
defaultDirections: Take 1 to 2 tablets once daily with food. Do not exceed 5mg/kg/day.

commonDoses.label: Standard daily dose (200mg daily)
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet daily with dinner.

commonDoses.label: Higher daily dose (400mg daily)
commonDoses.directions: Take 2 tablets daily with food (if actual weight > 80kg).

warningNote: Requires baseline and periodic ophthalmologic screening for irreversible maculopathy.

name: Salazopyrin EN-tabs (sulfasalazine 500mg enteric-coated tablet)
indication: Rheumatoid arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, ulcerative colitis, Crohn's disease.
mechanismOfAction: Cleaved by colonic bacteria into sulfapyridine (active in arthritis) and 5-aminosalicylic acid (mesalazine, active in bowel wall).
counselingAdvice: Swallow whole with a full glass of water with meals; do not crush or chew. May cause orange-yellow discolouration of urine and soft contact lenses. Maintain abundant fluid intake.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in sulfonamide or salicylate allergy, intestinal or urinary obstruction, porphyria, severe renal/hepatic impairment.
adverseEffects: Nausea, dyspepsia, headache, reversible male oligospermia, skin rash, leukopenia, elevated liver enzymes.
monitoringAdvice: Full blood count and liver function tests every 2-4 weeks for the first 3 months, then 3-monthly.
defaultDirections: Take 2 tablets twice daily with meals. Swallow whole with water.

commonDoses.label: Maintenance dose (1g BD)
commonDoses.directions: Take 2 tablets morning and evening with food.

commonDoses.label: Initiation titration (500mg daily start)
commonDoses.directions: Take 1 tablet daily for week 1, increasing by 500mg weekly.

warningNote: Contraindicated with sulfa allergy; may discolour urine and contact lenses yellow-orange.

name: Trelegy Ellipta (fluticasone furoate 100mcg + umeclidinium 62.5mcg + vilanterol 25mcg inhaler 30 doses)
indication: Maintenance treatment of moderate to severe COPD not adequately treated by dual therapy; maintenance treatment of asthma in adults.
mechanismOfAction: Combines an inhaled corticosteroid (fluticasone furoate), a long-acting muscarinic antagonist (umeclidinium), and a long-acting beta-2 agonist (vilanterol) for 24-hour bronchodilation and anti-inflammatory control.
pbsRestrictionNote: Authority Required: Severe COPD with frequent exacerbations despite dual therapy.
counselingAdvice: Inhale 1 puff once daily at the same time each day. Rinse mouth with water and spit out after inhalation to prevent oral thrush and hoarseness.
cautionsAndContraindications: Not for acute relief of bronchospasm. Caution in severe cardiovascular disorders or narrow-angle glaucoma.
adverseEffects: Nasopharyngitis, headache, cough, oral candidiasis, dysphonia, pneumonia (in COPD), tachycardia.
monitoringAdvice: Assess lung function (spirometry) and monitor for symptoms of pneumonia in COPD patients.
storageAdvice: Store below 30°C in moisture-protective foil tray. Use within 6 weeks of opening tray.
defaultDirections: Inhale 1 blister once daily at the same time each day. Rinse and spit after use.

commonDoses.label: Once daily maintenance
commonDoses.directions: Inhale 1 dose once daily. Rinse mouth with water afterwards.

warningNote: Always rinse mouth and spit after use to prevent oral candidiasis.

name: Dymista (azelastine hydrochloride 137mcg + fluticasone propionate 50mcg nasal spray 120 doses)
indication: Relief of symptoms of moderate to severe allergic rhinitis and rhino-conjunctivitis.
mechanismOfAction: Dual mechanism: rapid H1-antihistamine blockade (azelastine) provides onset within 15 minutes; potent corticosteroid (fluticasone) suppresses ongoing late-phase inflammation.
counselingAdvice: Blow nose gently. Shake bottle well. Spray 1 spray into each nostril twice daily with head tilted slightly forward. May notice a transient bitter taste if sprayed backwards into the throat.
cautionsAndContraindications: Known hypersensitivity to components.
adverseEffects: Dysgeusia (bitter taste), epistaxis, headache, nasal discomfort, sneezing.
monitoringAdvice: Inspect nasal mucosa periodically during prolonged use.
storageAdvice: Store upright below 25°C. Do not refrigerate or freeze.
defaultDirections: Instil 1 spray into each nostril twice daily with head tilted forward.

commonDoses.label: Standard BD nasal regimen
commonDoses.directions: Instil 1 spray into each nostril morning and night.

name: Bricanyl Turbuhaler (terbutaline sulfate 500mcg/dose 100 doses)
indication: Relief of bronchospasm in bronchial asthma, chronic bronchitis, and emphysema.
mechanismOfAction: Stimulates beta-2 adrenergic receptors in bronchial smooth muscle, activating adenylate cyclase and producing bronchodilation within minutes.
counselingAdvice: Inhale as needed for acute shortness of breath or wheeze. If using more than 2-3 times per week, asthma preventer therapy needs escalation.
cautionsAndContraindications: Thyrotoxicosis, severe cardiovascular disease.
adverseEffects: Tremor, palpitations, headache, tachycardia, muscle cramps.
monitoringAdvice: Review reliever frequency; high usage indicates poorly controlled asthma.
storageAdvice: Store below 30°C with cap tightly screwed on.
defaultFrequency: As needed for relief of asthma symptoms
defaultDirections: Inhale 1 puff as needed for breathlessness. May repeat in 5 minutes if required.

commonDoses.label: PRN Reliever
commonDoses.directions: Inhale 1 to 2 puffs as needed for acute shortness of breath.

name: Atrovent (ipratropium bromide 20mcg/actuation inhaler 200 doses)
indication: Maintenance bronchodilator treatment of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and asthma.
mechanismOfAction: Competitively blocks muscarinic cholinergic receptors in bronchial smooth muscle, reducing vagally mediated bronchoconstriction.
counselingAdvice: Use with a spacer for best drug delivery. Avoid spraying into eyes (may cause pupil dilation or worsen narrow-angle glaucoma).
cautionsAndContraindications: Caution in narrow-angle glaucoma, prostatic hypertrophy, or bladder neck obstruction.
adverseEffects: Dry mouth, throat irritation, cough, urinary hesitancy, blurred vision.
monitoringAdvice: Assess symptom control in COPD.
storageAdvice: Store below 25°C. Protect from direct heat.
defaultDirections: Inhale 2 puffs 3 to 4 times daily, ideally via a spacer device.

commonDoses.label: Standard COPD dosing
commonDoses.directions: Inhale 2 puffs 4 times daily using a spacer.
